11	## Contexto y problema
12	
13	El PDF exige que "no Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser" y "public role permissions minimal and justified". D4 (G0) fijó lo siguiente: rol público solo `find`/`findOne`, nginx como proxy GET-only con allowlist, ningún token en el navegador y sin BFF. Quedan por concretar cuatro cosas:
14	
15	1. Los permisos exactos y la allowlist.
16	2. Que "recargar" muestre siempre lo publicado: sin caché intermedia (Q-01.20, REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23).
17	3. Que nunca se sirvan borradores (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.2).
18	4. Cómo se prueban los AC que describen un cambio de contenido en Strapi (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.13, AC-01.31, AC-02.21, AC-02.25, AC-03.15, AC-03.19) sin romper el arranque con un solo comando ni introducir credenciales.
19	
20	### Hallazgo: el rol público puede leer borradores
21	
22	En Strapi 5, el parámetro `status` de la REST API admite `draft` y `published`, y el valor por defecto es `published`. **No hay un permiso separado para leer borradores.** Según la petición abierta en el portal de feedback de Strapi (3 de febrero de 2026), "any user with find or findOne permission on a content-type can access draft entries by using the status parameter". La documentación de Draft & Publish confirma que la Content API puede pedir "draft or published content" con `status`, y menciona además el parámetro `publicationFilter`. La página del parámetro `status` no dice qué permiso exige `status=draft` (verificación del orquestador en `reviews/001-G3-architecture-check.md`). Por eso el middleware se mantiene como defensa en profundidad, y su `curl` de confirmación es obligatorio al implementar.
23	
24	Consecuencia: con D4 tal como está, una petición pública `GET /api/plans?status=draft` podría devolver borradores (planes o términos sin publicar). La app nunca la hace (REQ-01.6), pero un visitante sí podría. D4 sigue siendo viable, pero necesita una medida adicional que no la contradice: forzar `published` en las rutas públicas.
25	
26	## Factores de decisión
27	
28	- Ningún token en el navegador ni en el bundle (`CLAUDE.md` §6).
29	- Superficie pública mínima: solo lo que leen US-01, US-02 y US-03 (api-contracts).
30	- Defensa en profundidad: un fallo en una capa (nginx, permisos de Strapi o código) no expone escritura ni borradores.
31	- Cambios visibles al recargar, sin caché HTTP intermedia.
32	- E2E reproducibles con `docker compose up` por cualquiera que clone el repositorio, sin pasos manuales ni credenciales (PDF: "a single command to start the whole project").
33	- Sin dependencias nuevas.
34	
35	## Opciones consideradas
36	
37	**Eje 1: cómo llega el navegador a Strapi**
38	
39	1. **1a. nginx mismo origen, GET-only con allowlist exacta y saneado de cabeceras (D4).**
40	2. **1b. Navegador directo a Strapi (`:1337`) con CORS.**
41	3. **1c. BFF propio** (Node) que llama a Strapi con credenciales de servidor.
42	
43	**Eje 2: cómo evitar borradores en lecturas públicas**
44	
45	1. **2a. Middleware de ruta en Strapi `published-only`** en las rutas `find` públicas, más un rechazo best-effort en nginx.
46	2. **2b. Solo nginx**: rechazar `status` y `publicationFilter` en la query.
47	3. **2c. Desactivar Draft & Publish** en los content types públicos.
48	4. **2d. Plugin de terceros** (`strapi-plugin-draft-preview`, opción `guardNativeStatus`).
49	
50	**Eje 3: cómo se prueban los AC de cambio de contenido** (G3-3)
51	
52	1. **3a. Escrituras reales en Strapi desde el proceso Node de Playwright** con un token de API Custom creado a mano en el admin.
53	2. **3b. Login de administrador automatizado** desde Playwright y uso de los endpoints internos del admin (Content Manager).
54	3. **3c. Solo intercepción de red** (`page.route`): el e2e modifica en el navegador de pruebas la respuesta real de Strapi.
55	4. **3d. Verificación manual** del cambio real en Strapi.
56	
57	## Decisión
58	
59	Opción elegida: **1a + 2a + 3c**, con **3d** para el cambio real en Strapi, que se comprueba a mano en G5 (G3-3).
60	
61	### 1. Rol público de Strapi (bootstrap idempotente)
62	
63	**Solo `find`**, sin `findOne`, en cuatro tipos (G3-2: precisión de D4, que fijaba `find`/`findOne` como máximo):
64	
65	| Permiso | Motivo | Lecturas que lo usan |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| `api::country.country.find` | Lista de países (`/`, "país no disponible"), configuración del país, factores, términos | C1, C3, C6, C7 (api-contracts) |
68	| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Campos del paso 1 del país | C4 |
69	| `api::plan.plan.find` | Planes del país | C5 |
70	| `api::country-selection.country-selection.find` | Textos de `/` | C2 |
71	
72	- **No se concede `findOne`** en ningún tipo: ninguna lectura lo necesita (el plan elegido se comprueba contra la lista, REQ-03.14).
73	- El bootstrap **elimina cualquier otro permiso** del rol público (incluidos los de `plugin::users-permissions.auth.*` y los de `upload`) y desactiva el registro de usuarios ("Enable sign-ups" = false) en los ajustes avanzados de Users & Permissions. Es idempotente: en cada arranque deja exactamente esta tabla.
74	- Ningún tipo usa i18n (ADR-0001). El rol `authenticated` no tiene permisos.
75	
76	### 2. nginx (único punto de entrada del navegador)
77	
78	- Sirve el build de Angular y hace de proxy de `/api` hacia Strapi en la red interna de Docker. El puerto de Strapi se publica solo en `127.0.0.1:1337`, para el admin del negocio. El admin de Strapi no pasa por nginx.
79	- **Allowlist exacta** con `location =`:
80	  - `/api/countries`
81	  - `/api/form-fields`
82	  - `/api/plans`
83	  - `/api/country-selection`
84	- `location /api/` → `404` para todo lo demás: `findOne` (`/api/plans/<id>`), `/api/auth/*`, `/api/upload`, `/api/users`...
85	- En cada `location` permitida, `limit_except GET { deny all; }`. Según la documentación de nginx, permitir `GET` también permite `HEAD`; cualquier otro método recibe `403`.
86	- **Saneado de la petición:** `proxy_set_header Authorization "";` y `proxy_set_header Cookie "";`. Aunque una cabecera llegara desde el navegador, nunca se reenvía.
87	- **Rechazo best-effort de borradores:** `if ($args ~* "(^|&)(status|publicationFilter)(=|%5B|\[)") { return 400; }`. Es *best-effort* porque `$args` es la query sin decodificar y una clave codificada (`%73tatus`) la sortearía. La garantía real es el middleware de Strapi.
88	- **Caché:**
89	  - En `/api/*`: `proxy_hide_header Cache-Control; proxy_hide_header Expires; add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;` y ningún `proxy_cache`.
90	  - `index.html`: `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
91	  - Bundles con hash del build: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
92	  - Como `add_header` solo se hereda si el nivel actual no define ninguno (documentación de nginx), las cabeceras de seguridad se repiten en cada `location` que defina `add_header`.
93	- **Cabeceras de seguridad del SPA:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` y `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` es el fallback que documenta Angular para hosts estáticos sin nonce por petición (Angular inserta `<style>` de componentes). Si el build inserta scripts o manejadores inline (p. ej. `onload` del CSS crítico), se activa `autoCsp` o se desactiva la inlinización de CSS crítico; lo decide el Angular Developer al verificar la CSP en el navegador.
94	
95	### 3. Strapi: solo lectura publicada en la Content API (2a)
96	
97	- Middleware de ruta `global::published-only` (`cms/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`), referenciado en `config.find.middlewares` del `createCoreRouter` de los cuatro tipos públicos. Antes de llamar a `next()`, sustituye `ctx.query.status` por `'published'` y elimina `ctx.query.publicationFilter`. Se aplica a todas las peticiones `find` de esos tipos.
98	- Como ningún cliente escribe por la Content API (ni la app, ni los e2e, ver §5), los cuatro routers se declaran con **`only: ['find']`**. Las rutas `findOne`, `create`, `update` y `delete` de la Content API no se cargan. El admin de Strapi no se ve afectado, porque usa su propia API, no estas rutas.
99	- Configuración de la REST API (`cms/config/api.ts`): `defaultLimit: 25`, `maxLimit: 100` explícitos, para que la paginación del contrato (pageSize 100) sea predecible.
100	
101	### 4. Angular
102	
103	- `CmsClient` usa URLs relativas (`/api/...`) y `HttpClient` sin interceptores de autenticación. **No existe ninguna variable, constante ni `environment` con credenciales.**
104	- En desarrollo, `ng serve` usa `proxy.conf.json` hacia nginx (`http://localhost:8080`), no hacia Strapi, para probar la misma allowlist.
105	- No hay caché persistente de contenido: ni `localStorage`, ni `sessionStorage`, ni service worker (`@angular/service-worker` no se instala). La configuración del país se guarda en memoria durante la carga de la app (ADR-0004).
106	- El pago simulado no hace ninguna petición (REQ-03.20).
107	
108	### 5. AC de cambio de contenido: intercepción (3c) y comprobación manual en G5 (3d)
109	
110	**Mecanismo.** El e2e no escribe en Strapi ni usa ninguna credencial. Para simular "el negocio publica un cambio y recargo":
111	
112	1. Carga la página contra el Strapi real con el seed.
113	2. Registra `page.route` sobre la petición afectada. El manejador obtiene la **respuesta real** con `route.fetch()`, aplica solo el cambio del escenario sobre su JSON y la devuelve con `route.fulfill({ response, body })`.
114	3. Recarga y comprueba la UI.
115	
116	Así solo se simula el cambio; el resto de la respuesta (formato v5, `documentId`, componentes) es el de Strapi.
117	
118	| AC | Cambio que aplica la intercepción |
119	|---|---|
120	| AC-01.3 | C4: añade un campo publicado nuevo |
121	| AC-01.10 | C4: quita el campo A e intercambia el `order` de B y C |
122	| AC-01.11 | Sin intercepción: el **seed incluye un campo en borrador por país** (content-model §6), y el e2e comprueba contra Strapi real que no aparece y que ninguna petición de la app lleva `status` o `publicationFilter` |
123	| AC-01.13 (2.ª parte) | C4: añade la opción "Marca C" al `select` de marca |
124	| AC-01.31 | C3: cambia `formStepTexts.continueLabel` solo en la respuesta de CL; CO sin cambios |
125	| AC-02.21, AC-03.19 | C5: quita de la lista el plan persistido (desactivado o despublicado) o cambia su `currency` |
126	| AC-02.25 | C5 o C6: cambia el orden, el recomendado, el precio base de un plan, o una banda de `priceFactors` |
127	| AC-03.15 | C7: cambia `termsAndConditions` de CL |
128	
129	La intercepción cubre también los casos que Strapi no permite publicar o los fallos: texto obligatorio ausente (AC-01.35, AC-02.33, AC-03.36; G3-5), tipo desconocido o campo sin label (AC-01.25), moneda distinta (AC-02.14), plan sin precio (AC-02.15), 30 planes (AC-02.32), errores y latencia (AC-01.7, AC-01.8, AC-02.23, AC-02.24, AC-03.16, AC-03.17) y términos con HTML (AC-03.14).
130	
131	**Comprobación manual en G5 (G3-3).** Con la pila levantada, el humano:
132	
133	1. Añade y publica en el admin de Strapi un campo nuevo para un país, recarga la app y comprueba que aparece (AC-01.3).
134	2. Desactiva un plan, recarga el paso de planes y comprueba que ya no aparece (AC-02.25).
135	3. Restaura ambos cambios.
136	
137	El resultado se registra en `docs/qa/manual-check.md`. El informe de e2e indica que la integración real Strapi → app para esos AC se verifica en esa comprobación.
138	
139	## Consecuencias
140	
141	- **Positivas:**
142	  - Tres capas independientes:
143	    - nginx: GET-only, allowlist y sin `Authorization`.
144	    - Permisos: solo `find` en cuatro tipos, y routers con `only: ['find']`.
145	    - Middleware de Strapi: solo publicado.
146	  - Un error en una de ellas no expone escritura ni borradores.
147	  - No existe ninguna credencial de escritura en el proyecto: ni en `.env`, ni en `e2e/`, ni en el frontend. La superficie del requisito de seguridad del PDF se reduce a cero.
148	  - Todos los e2e se ejecutan con `docker compose up` y `npx playwright test`, sin pasos previos. Ningún AC queda "No ejecutado" para quien clone el repositorio.
149	  - Los e2e no modifican la base de datos de la demo y pueden correr en paralelo.
150	  - "Recargar" siempre pide a Strapi y nada intermedio guarda respuestas (Q-01.20).
151	- **Negativas:**
152	  - Los escenarios del PDF "Configuration change without deployment" (AC-01.3) y el cambio de planes (AC-02.25) **no se prueban de forma automática contra un cambio real en Strapi**. Lo automatizado prueba que la app refleja una respuesta distinta al recargar. Que Strapi produzca esa respuesta tras publicar se comprueba una vez a mano en G5, y esa evidencia no se repite en cada ejecución.
153	  - `route.fetch()` + modificación depende de que el e2e conozca la forma del JSON (api-contracts). Si el contrato cambia, hay que actualizar las pruebas.
154	  - Despublicar desde el admin solo se comprueba de forma indirecta (borradores del seed y comprobación manual).
155	  - `no-store` impide cualquier caché del navegador para `/api`. Con este volumen no importa, pero cada recarga cuesta todas las peticiones.
156	  - `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` debilita la CSP frente a la inyección de estilos (es la alternativa documentada sin nonce).
157	  - El middleware `published-only` y `only: ['find']` son código propio en `cms/`: si un content type público nuevo no los referencia, queda expuesto. Lo vigila un punto de la checklist de review.
158	- **Riesgos y mitigación:**
159	  - *`ctx.query` aún no está procesado cuando corre el middleware de ruta* (la documentación no lo precisa). Se comprueba con la confirmación de abajo. Si falla, se usa un middleware global registrado en `config/middlewares.ts` después de `strapi::query`.
160	  - *Exposición del admin de Strapi:* solo en `127.0.0.1`. El admin usa su propia sesión, que es el uso previsto de Strapi y no forma parte de la app pública.
161	
162	### Confirmación
163	
164	- Con la pila levantada (`docker compose up`):
165	  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/plans` → `403`
166	  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/api/plans/abc` → `404`
167	  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:8080/api/plans?status=draft"` → `400`
168	  - `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans?status=draft"` (directo a Strapi) → solo planes publicados: el seed tiene un borrador por país (REQ-02.33) que **no** debe aparecer. Igual con `/api/form-fields?status=draft` y el campo en borrador del seed
169	  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans` → `404` o `405` (ruta no cargada por `only: ['find']`)
170	  - `curl -sI http://localhost:8080/api/countries` → incluye `Cache-Control: no-store`
171	- E2E AC-01.30, AC-02.31 y AC-03.24: ninguna petición de la página lleva `Authorization`, y todas las de `/api` son `GET`.
172	- G5: `docs/qa/manual-check.md` registra la comprobación manual del campo nuevo y del plan desactivado.
173	- Review (checklist de seguridad):
174	  - `grep -rniE "authorization|bearer|api[_-]?token" frontend/ e2e/` → solo la aserción de AC-01.30 en `e2e/` (comprueba la *ausencia* de la cabecera).
175	  - `.env.example` no contiene ninguna variable de token de Strapi.
176	  - Los permisos públicos del bootstrap coinciden con la tabla.
177	  - Cada router público tiene `only: ['find']` y referencia `global::published-only`.
178	
179	## Pros y contras de las opciones
180	
181	### 1a. nginx mismo origen (elegida, D4)
182	
183	- A favor: sin CORS; una única superficie pública controlable; sanea cabeceras; sirve el SPA y la API desde el mismo origen.
184	- En contra: allowlist duplicada respecto a los permisos (dos sitios que mantener).
185	
186	### 1b. Navegador directo a Strapi
187	
188	- A favor: un componente menos.
189	- En contra: expone todas las rutas de Strapi (admin incluido) al navegador, exige CORS y no permite limitar métodos ni cabeceras; contradice D4.
190	
191	### 1c. BFF
192	
193	- A favor: podría ocultar Strapi por completo y validar parámetros.
194	- En contra: más código y más infraestructura; D4 lo excluye de forma explícita.
195	
196	### 2a. Middleware `published-only` en Strapi (elegida) + nginx best-effort
197	
198	- A favor: actúa sobre la query ya interpretada por Strapi, no sobre la cadena cruda; no depende de terceros.
199	- En contra: código propio que hay que referenciar en cada router público.
200	
201	### 2b. Solo nginx
202	
203	- A favor: cero código en Strapi.
204	- En contra: se sortea codificando la clave del parámetro, y no protege el acceso directo a `127.0.0.1:1337`.
205	
206	### 2c. Sin Draft & Publish
207	
208	- A favor: elimina el problema de raíz.
209	- En contra: **incumple** el PDF ("only published and active plans") y AC-01.11 y AC-02.5, que exigen borradores.
210	
211	### 2d. Plugin de terceros
212	
213	- A favor: resuelve el caso con una opción.
214	- En contra: dependencia nueva de un tercero para una regla de seguridad, mantenida fuera de Strapi; el middleware equivalente es breve.
215	
216	### 3a. Escrituras reales con token Custom (descartada en G3-3)
217	
218	- A favor: prueba de forma automática la integración real Strapi → app con la Content API documentada. El token tendría alcance mínimo, nunca tocaría el navegador y se podría revocar.
219	- En contra (motivo del descarte):
220	  - Strapi no documenta cómo crear tokens por código, así que habría que crearlo **a mano** en el admin. Es un paso manual que choca con el arranque con un solo comando que pide el PDF.
221	  - Para quien clone el repositorio sin ese token, **5 AC quedarían "No ejecutados"** (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.31 y AC-02.25).
222	  - Además, añadiría una credencial de escritura al proyecto, tests que mutan la base de la demo, ejecución en serie con restauración, y despublicado simulado con borrados.

226	- A favor: totalmente automático; permitiría despublicar de verdad con el Content Manager.
227	- En contra: depende de **endpoints internos no documentados** del admin, que pueden cambiar entre versiones menores. Exigiría credenciales de superadministrador en el entorno de pruebas, con mucho más alcance que cualquier token. Las alternativas oficiales (tokens de admin) también se crean a mano.

230	
231	- A favor: sin credenciales ni pasos manuales; determinista y rápida; reproducible por cualquiera que clone el repositorio; con `route.fetch()` solo se simula el cambio y el resto de la respuesta es la real.
232	- En contra: no prueba de forma automática que Strapi produzca la respuesta tras publicar. Se compensa con 3d en G5.
233	
234	### 3d. Verificación manual (complemento de 3c, G5)
235	
236	- A favor: comprueba la integración real con el admin, incluido publicar y desactivar.
237	- En contra: no es repetible en cada ejecución; la evidencia es un registro manual.
238

# ADR-0002 — Dynamic step 1 form with Signal Forms

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
| Date | 2026-11-22 |
| Author | Software Architect (subagent) |
| Deciders | Human (G3) |
| Motivated by | D5, D2 · G2-1, G2-4, G2-5, G2-7, G2-13 · REQ-01.7, REQ-01.8, REQ-01.10, REQ-01.11, REQ-01.14, REQ-01.15, REQ-01.16, REQ-01.17, REQ-01.19, REQ-01.20, REQ-01.21, REQ-01.22, REQ-01.29, REQ-01.30 |

## Context and problem

Step 1 is generated at runtime from the country's configuration in Strapi: the fields, their type (`text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`), whether they are required, their typed validations (G2-7 catalog), their role (G2-1) and a single error message per field. D5 set Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`), which the official comparison table marks as "Stable (v22+)". This ADR specifies how to build that form when the keys and the rules arrive over HTTP, and which parts of the API are used.

## Decision drivers

- The configuration arrives asynchronously and changes without deploying (REQ-01.6).
- Typed validations from a closed catalog, plus role rules that are always active (G2-4, G2-5).
- One message per field, visible when leaving the field or when trying to advance (REQ-01.16).
- Pure functions testable without Angular (`CLAUDE.md` §8; REQ-01.21).
- Accessibility: `<label>`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, focus on the first invalid field (REQ-01.17, REQ-01.29).
- Use only stable API in v22, with no new dependencies.

## API verification (angular.dev, 2026-11-22)

| Need | Signal Forms API | Verified status |
|---|---|---|
| Create the form from a model | `form(model, schema, options)` | Stable since v22.0 |
| Create the form outside the constructor | `FormOptions.injector` | Stable since v22.0 (`FormOptions` interface) |
| Bind a native control | `FormField` directive, `formField` input (`[formField]="..."`) | Stable since v22.0 |
| Submit from `<form>` (including Enter) | `[formRoot]` + `FormOptions.submission` (`action`, `onInvalid`) | "Form submission" guide: `FormRoot` sets `novalidate`, prevents navigation and calls `submit` if there is a `submission` option |
| Dynamic keys | `Record<string, ...>` model + schema that iterates over the configuration | Official "Dynamic forms with JSON" guide |
| Built-in validators | `required`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern` | "Validation" guide |
| Custom validators | `validate(path, ({ value }) => error \| null)` | "Validation" guide |
| Per-field state | `value()`, `valid()`, `invalid()`, `errors()`, `touched()`, `markAsTouched()` | "Field state management" guide: `touched()` becomes `true` on focus and blur |
| Mark everything as touched on submit | `submit()` marks the interactive fields as touched | "Form submission" guide |
| Focus a field | `fieldTree().focusBoundControl()` | "Form submission" guide (`onInvalid` example) |
| Native types | text, number (converts between string and number), checkbox (boolean), select with dynamic options, date | "Forms with signals" guide (essentials). `<select multiple>` is not supported |

**Documentation gaps to check with a spike when starting US-01** (none blocks the decision):

1. **Value of an empty `<input type="number">`.** The dynamic forms guide initializes numeric fields to `null`, but does not document which value the control writes when it is emptied (`null` or `NaN`). The `required` validator treats `null`, `undefined`, `''`, `false` and `NaN` as empty, so either works, and the output mapper normalizes `NaN` to `null`.
2. **`<input type="date">` with a `string` model.** The guide says date controls "also accept `Date`", but not whether they keep a `YYYY-MM-DD` `string`. A `string` is required so the date is not shifted by time zone (REQ-01.21; the validation guide itself warns about the shift with `Date`). If the spike shows that the control writes a `Date`, a custom control implementing `FormValueControl<string>` is used ("Custom controls" guide), with no dependencies.
3. **`aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.** The `FormField` reference does not say it sets them, so they are bound manually in the template.

No required API is marked as experimental. The only experimental property found (`FormOptions.experimentalWebMcpTool`) is not used.

## Considered options

1. **Signal Forms with a flat `Record<key, FieldValue>` model and a schema generated from the configuration**, following the official "Dynamic forms with JSON" guide.
2. **Signal Forms with a model nested by section** (`{ policyholder: {...}, vehicle: {...} }`).
3. **Typed Reactive Forms** (`FormRecord` + `ValidatorFn`).
4. **Custom form using only `signal`/`computed`**, without `@angular/forms`.

Sub-decision on **how to model the validations in Strapi** (affects the contract):

- **V1.** Repeatable component `form.validation-rule` with `kind` (enum) and parameters `value` (decimal) and `pattern` (string).
- **V2.** Dynamic zone with one component per validation type.
- **V3.** Free-form JSON field.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1 (Signal Forms, flat model) + V1**.

### Construction

1. `FormStepPage` waits until the country configuration is ready (ADR-0004). Only then does it render `DynamicForm` with the already mapped configuration (`FormConfig`) as `input.required`.
2. `DynamicForm` creates the form in `ngOnInit` (the inputs are already available) with `form(model, buildStep1Schema(config, ctx), { injector, submission })`. The `injector` is obtained with `inject(Injector)` in the class field. The configuration is treated as immutable during the component's lifetime: if it is reloaded (retry), the component is recreated because the `@if` destroys it.
3. **Model:** `signal<Step1Model>()`, where `Step1Model = Record<FieldKey, string | number | boolean | null>`. Initial values by type: `text` → `''`, `number` → `null`, `select` → `''`, `date` → `''`, `checkbox` → `false`. The restored and reconciled values are applied on top of them (ADR-0004). Keys match `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` (content-model), so `Object.keys` keeps insertion order, although the screen order does not depend on it.
4. **Typed accessors** by type (`asText(key): FieldTree<string>`, `asNumber`, `asBoolean`...), with the deliberate cast documented by the official guide ("deliberate escape hatches"). The cast is covered by a mapper test: the field type determines the initial value.
5. **Template:** `<form [formRoot]="f">`, `@for (section of sections(); track section.id)` inside `<fieldset><legend>`, and `@for (field of section.fields; track field.key)` with a `@switch (field.type)` that renders the native control with `[formField]`. `select`: `<select>` with a first empty `<option value="">`, with no text (G2-2 and Q-01.17: there are no placeholders), and the options in Strapi order.

### Validation (generated schema)

For each field of the configuration, in order:

| Source | How it is applied | Pure function (no Angular) |
|---|---|---|
| `required` (Strapi) | built-in `required(path)` (reflects `required` on the native control) and, for `text`, also `validate(path, notBlank)` | `isBlank(value)`: a text of only spaces counts as empty (REQ-01.14). Required `checkbox` = `true`, which the built-in `required` already covers because it treats `false` as empty |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` (`text`) | `validate(path, ...)` | `hasMinLength(trimmed, n)`, `hasMaxLength(trimmed, n)` on the trimmed value (Q-01.16) |
| `pattern` (`text`) | `validate(path, ...)` | `matchesFully(trimmed, regex)`. The mapper compiles `new RegExp('^(?:' + source + ')$')` without flags; if it does not compile, the validation is ignored with a warning (5.3) |
| `min` / `max` / `integer` (`number`) | `validate(path, ...)` | `isAtLeast`, `isAtMost`, `isInteger` |
| `vehicleYear` role (`number`) | `validate(path, ...)`, always active | `isVehicleYearValid(year, today)`: `year(today) − 20 ≤ year ≤ year(today) + 1`, integer (REQ-01.19) |
| `birthDate` role (`date`) | `validate(path, ...)`, always active | `isOfLegalAge(birthDate, today, minimumAge)`, with a future date invalid and the February 29 rule (REQ-01.20) |
| `select` | implicit `validate(path, ...)` | The value, if not empty, must be a current option |

- Custom validators **are not reimplemented on top of the built-in ones** when these do not trim spaces (`minLength`, `pattern`). That is why pure functions wrapped in `validate()` are used. They all live in `frontend/src/app/domain/` and `features/form-step/validation/`, and have unit tests named by AC (AC-01.14, AC-01.15, AC-01.17, AC-01.18, AC-01.19, AC-01.33).
- **"Today"** is obtained from a `CLOCK` token (`() => Date`) and converted into a local `YYYY-MM-DD` date (`todayLocal`). The validators receive the date as a parameter (REQ-01.21).
- The error `kind` is never shown. **A single message per field** (REQ-01.16): `field.errorMessage` if it is not empty and, if it is, the country's generic message.
- **Error visibility:** `state.touched() && state.invalid()`. `touched()` becomes `true` when leaving the field (blur) and `submit()` marks all interactive fields. Interpretation of "not while typing" (REQ-01.16): the error does not appear before the first blur or the first attempt to advance. After that it updates live, so it disappears as soon as the value is valid. If the human prefers to freeze it until the next blur, it is a local change (an `errorShown` signal per field) that does not affect this decision.
- **G2-5 (REQ-01.22)** is not validated in the form: the configuration mapper decides it. If a valid field with one of the required roles is missing, `FormConfig.status = 'unavailable'` and `DynamicForm` is never created.

### Submission, advancing and focus

- `submission.action`: saves the normalized values (ADR-0004) and navigates to `/:country/plans`.
- `submission.onInvalid`: walks the ordered list of fields (section and then `order`), finds the first one with `invalid()` and calls `focusBoundControl()`. `errorSummary()` is not used for the order, because the screen order is defined by the configuration (REQ-01.17).
- Enter in a text field submits the `<form>` natively, which is equivalent to "continue" (REQ-01.30). The continue button is `type="submit"` and is always enabled.

### Accessibility (manual bindings)

- Control `id` `f-{key}`; `<label for="f-{key}">`; help `help-{key}`; error `err-{key}`.
- `[attr.aria-describedby]` with `help-{key}` and, only if the error is visible, `err-{key}`. `[attr.aria-invalid]` is `'true'` or `null`. For `checkbox` and `select` the native `required` is set by `FormField`, and it is checked in a DOM unit test.

### Validations in Strapi (V1)

Repeatable component `form.validation-rule { kind: enumeration[minLength, maxLength, pattern, min, max, integer], value: decimal?, pattern: string? }` inside `form-field.validations`. The mapper checks that each rule has the parameters of its `kind` and that the `kind` matches the field type (5.2 and 5.3). Whatever does not fit is ignored with a warning.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - It follows the pattern documented by Angular for JSON-driven forms, with stable API in v22.
  - All business logic stays in pure functions with deterministic tests. The schema is just an adapter.
  - Changing a field, the order, an option or a catalog validation in Strapi requires no code (case A of `country-content`). A new validation type is a localized case B: one value in the `kind` enum, one pure function and one line in the registry.
  - The flat model by key fits the persistence by technical identifier (ADR-0004) and the reconciliation of 5.4. Moving a field to another section does not move the value.
- **Negative:**
  - The typed accessor casts trade the compiler's structural guarantee for a runtime invariant (the guide itself warns about this). It is mitigated with tests of the mapper and of the initial value by type.
  - The form does not react to hot configuration changes: it has to be recreated. This is consistent with Q-01.20 (one load per app reload).
  - Signal Forms is stable only since v22 and there are fewer community examples and answers than for Reactive Forms. There are three documentation gaps that require a spike.
  - With V1, the admin shows the `value` and `pattern` fields for any `kind`, and the business can fill in the wrong one. The mapper ignores it with a warning, but the business gets no warning in the admin.
  - The `kind` catalog is duplicated (Strapi enum and TypeScript type).
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *ReDoS from a malicious `pattern`:* the pattern is written by a trusted team in the admin (US-01 §7). The risk is accepted and documented.
  - *The spike results contradict an assumption:* the alternatives are local (custom control with `FormValueControl`) and do not change the decision. If a real Signal Forms blocker appeared, option 3 requires a new decision log entry replacing D5.

### Confirmation

- Unit: validator registry (AC-01.14, AC-01.15, AC-01.33), role rules with an injected date (AC-01.17, AC-01.18 and AC-01.19 with `TZ=America/Bogota`, ADR-0007), mapper (AC-01.20, AC-01.25) and form DOM (AC-01.26: `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `fieldset`/`legend`).
- E2E: AC-01.2, AC-01.12, AC-01.16 (focus on the first invalid field) and AC-01.27 (keyboard only and Enter).
- Review: `grep -rE "ReactiveFormsModule|FormGroup|FormControl|NgModel" frontend/src` with no results; no error text written in the code.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Signal Forms, flat model (chosen)

- For: meets D5; official pattern; stable keys; reactive validation without subscriptions; fits zoneless.
- Against: casts in the accessors; young API; documentation gaps (empty number, date as string).

### 2. Signal Forms, model nested by section

- For: the model structure mirrors the screen, and the summary could read the sections directly.
- Against: if the business changes a field's section, its value changes path in the model. That complicates the reconciliation (5.4 says a section change keeps the value) and the persistence. The section order is fixed and can be derived without nesting.

### 3. Typed Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`)

- For: mature and well-documented API for dynamic forms; hot `addControl`/`removeControl`; the official comparison recommends it for "complex, dynamic forms" when proven stability is needed.
- Against: **contradicts D5**. It mixes Observables with state that is signals in the rest of the app. It would only be considered as a contingency plan with a new human decision.

### 4. Custom form with signals

- For: full control and no new API to learn.
- Against: it reimplements `touched`, submission, the native attributes and focus; more code to maintain and test; contradicts D5.

### V1. Repeatable component with `kind` (chosen)

- For: simple populate (`populate[n]=validations`); order and list visible in a single admin block; all rules share the same shape, so the mapper is simple.
- Against: irrelevant parameters visible depending on the `kind`; consistency is checked by the app and not by Strapi.

### V2. Dynamic zone, one component per validation type

- For: each type shows only its parameters; typing is stricter in the admin.
- Against: `integer` has no parameters, and a component without attributes is not documented as valid. Populating dynamic zones with several components is more verbose (`populate[dz][on][...]`). The filters documentation states that you cannot filter by dynamic zones (not needed here, but it limits evolution).

### V3. Free-form JSON

- For: maximum flexibility.
- Against: it is not "typed" (the PDF requires it and US-01 §6 forbids it: "no como texto libre"); the admin does not help the business.

## References

Consulted on 2026-11-22:

- Signal Forms, comparison ("Stable (v22+)" status): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/comparison
- Signal Forms, overview (imports, `FormField`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/overview
- Dynamic forms with JSON (`Record` model, schema in a loop, `[formField]`, `[formRoot]`, casts): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/dynamic-forms-with-json
- Validation (built-in validators, `validate`, error shape, `touched() && invalid()`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/validation
- Field state (`touched` on blur, `markAsTouched`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/field-state-management
- Submission (`submit`, `FormRoot`, `onInvalid`, `focusBoundControl`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/form-submission
- Models (`undefined` excluded from the tree, `null` for empty values, date controls and `Date`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/models
- Native controls (number, checkbox, dynamic select, no `select multiple`): https://angular.dev/essentials/signal-forms
- Custom controls (`FormValueControl`, `FormCheckboxControl`): https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/custom-controls
- `form` API (stable since v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/form
- `FormOptions` API (`injector`, `submission`; `experimentalWebMcpTool` experimental): https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/FormOptions
- `FormField` API (`formField` input, stable since v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/FormField
- Strapi 5, populate of components and dynamic zones: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select
- Strapi 5, filters (no filtering by dynamic zones): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/filters

> Translated into English on 2026-11-23 (D16); no content change.

# ADR-0003 — Strapi access, security, caching and content changes in the e2e tests

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
| Date | 2026-11-22 |
| Author | Software Architect (subagent) |
| Deciders | Human (G3) |
| Motivated by | D4, D9 · G2-13 (Q-01.20) · G3-2, G3-3 · REQ-01.6, REQ-01.35, REQ-02.2, REQ-02.23, REQ-02.31, REQ-03.20, REQ-03.24 · AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.13, AC-01.30, AC-01.31, AC-02.21, AC-02.25, AC-02.31, AC-03.15, AC-03.19, AC-03.24 |

## Context and problem

The PDF requires that "no Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser" and "public role permissions minimal and justified". D4 (G0) set the following: public role with only `find`/`findOne`, nginx as a GET-only proxy with an allowlist, no token in the browser and no BFF. Four things remain to be specified:

1. The exact permissions and the allowlist.
2. That "reload" always shows what is published: no intermediate cache (Q-01.20, REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23).
3. That drafts are never served (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.2).
4. How to test the ACs that describe a content change in Strapi (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.13, AC-01.31, AC-02.21, AC-02.25, AC-03.15, AC-03.19) without breaking the single-command startup or introducing credentials.

### Finding: the public role can read drafts

In Strapi 5, the REST API `status` parameter accepts `draft` and `published`, and the default value is `published`. **There is no separate permission for reading drafts.** According to the open request on the Strapi feedback portal (February 3, 2026), "any user with find or findOne permission on a content-type can access draft entries by using the status parameter". The Draft & Publish documentation confirms that the Content API can request "draft or published content" with `status`, and also mentions the `publicationFilter` parameter. The `status` parameter page does not say which permission `status=draft` requires (orchestrator verification in `reviews/001-G3-architecture-check.md`). That is why the middleware is kept as defense in depth, and its confirmation `curl` is mandatory during implementation.

Consequence: with D4 as it stands, a public `GET /api/plans?status=draft` request could return drafts (unpublished plans or terms). The app never makes it (REQ-01.6), but a visitor could. D4 remains viable, but it needs an additional measure that does not contradict it: forcing `published` on the public routes.

## Decision drivers

- No token in the browser or in the bundle (`CLAUDE.md` §6).
- Minimal public surface: only what US-01, US-02 and US-03 read (api-contracts).
- Defense in depth: a failure in one layer (nginx, Strapi permissions or code) does not expose writes or drafts.
- Changes visible on reload, with no intermediate HTTP cache.
- E2E tests reproducible with `docker compose up` by anyone who clones the repository, without manual steps or credentials (PDF: "a single command to start the whole project").
- No new dependencies.

## Considered options

**Axis 1: how the browser reaches Strapi**

1. **1a. nginx same origin, GET-only with an exact allowlist and header sanitization (D4).**
2. **1b. Browser directly to Strapi (`:1337`) with CORS.**
3. **1c. Custom BFF** (Node) that calls Strapi with server credentials.

**Axis 2: how to avoid drafts in public reads**

1. **2a. Strapi route middleware `published-only`** on the public `find` routes, plus a best-effort rejection in nginx.
2. **2b. nginx only**: reject `status` and `publicationFilter` in the query.
3. **2c. Disable Draft & Publish** on the public content types.
4. **2d. Third-party plugin** (`strapi-plugin-draft-preview`, `guardNativeStatus` option).

**Axis 3: how the content-change ACs are tested** (G3-3)

1. **3a. Real writes to Strapi from the Playwright Node process** with a Custom API token created by hand in the admin.
2. **3b. Automated administrator login** from Playwright and use of the admin's internal endpoints (Content Manager).
3. **3c. Network interception only** (`page.route`): the e2e modifies Strapi's real response in the test browser.
4. **3d. Manual verification** of the real change in Strapi.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1a + 2a + 3c**, with **3d** for the real change in Strapi, which is checked by hand in G5 (G3-3).

### 1. Strapi public role (idempotent bootstrap)

**Only `find`**, without `findOne`, on four types (G3-2: a refinement of D4, which set `find`/`findOne` as the maximum):

| Permission | Reason | Reads that use it |
|---|---|---|
| `api::country.country.find` | Country list (`/`, "país no disponible"), country configuration, factors, terms | C1, C3, C6, C7 (api-contracts) |
| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | The country's step 1 fields | C4 |
| `api::plan.plan.find` | The country's plans | C5 |
| `api::country-selection.country-selection.find` | `/` texts | C2 |

- **`findOne` is not granted** on any type: no read needs it (the chosen plan is checked against the list, REQ-03.14).
- The bootstrap **removes any other permission** from the public role (including those of `plugin::users-permissions.auth.*` and those of `upload`) and disables user registration ("Enable sign-ups" = false) in the Users & Permissions advanced settings. It is idempotent: on every startup it leaves exactly this table.
- No type uses i18n (ADR-0001). The `authenticated` role has no permissions.

### 2. nginx (the browser's only entry point)

- Serves the Angular build and proxies `/api` to Strapi on the internal Docker network. The Strapi port is published only on `127.0.0.1:1337`, for the business admin. The Strapi admin does not go through nginx.
- **Exact allowlist** with `location =`:
  - `/api/countries`
  - `/api/form-fields`
  - `/api/plans`
  - `/api/country-selection`
- `location /api/` → `404` for everything else: `findOne` (`/api/plans/<id>`), `/api/auth/*`, `/api/upload`, `/api/users`...
- In each allowed `location`, `limit_except GET { deny all; }`. According to the nginx documentation, allowing `GET` also allows `HEAD`; any other method receives `403`.
- **Request sanitization:** `proxy_set_header Authorization "";` and `proxy_set_header Cookie "";`. Even if a header arrived from the browser, it is never forwarded.
- **Best-effort draft rejection:** `if ($args ~* "(^|&)(status|publicationFilter)(=|%5B|\[)") { return 400; }`. It is *best-effort* because `$args` is the undecoded query and an encoded key (`%73tatus`) would bypass it. The real guarantee is the Strapi middleware.
- **Caching:**
  - On `/api/*`: `proxy_hide_header Cache-Control; proxy_hide_header Expires; add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;` and no `proxy_cache`.
  - `index.html`: `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
  - Build bundles with a hash: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  - Since `add_header` is only inherited if the current level defines none (nginx documentation), the security headers are repeated in every `location` that defines `add_header`.
- **SPA security headers:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is the fallback Angular documents for static hosts without a per-request nonce (Angular inserts component `<style>` elements). If the build inserts inline scripts or handlers (e.g. the critical CSS `onload`), `autoCsp` is enabled or critical CSS inlining is disabled; the Angular Developer decides this when verifying the CSP in the browser.

### 3. Strapi: published-only reads in the Content API (2a)

- Route middleware `global::published-only` (`cms/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`), referenced in `config.find.middlewares` of the `createCoreRouter` of the four public types. Before calling `next()`, it replaces `ctx.query.status` with `'published'` and removes `ctx.query.publicationFilter`. It applies to all `find` requests of those types.
- Since no client writes through the Content API (neither the app nor the e2e tests, see §5), the four routers are declared with **`only: ['find']`**. The Content API `findOne`, `create`, `update` and `delete` routes are not loaded. The Strapi admin is not affected, because it uses its own API, not these routes.
- REST API configuration (`cms/config/api.ts`): explicit `defaultLimit: 25`, `maxLimit: 100`, so that the contract's pagination (pageSize 100) is predictable.

### 4. Angular

- `CmsClient` uses relative URLs (`/api/...`) and `HttpClient` without authentication interceptors. **There is no variable, constant or `environment` with credentials.**
- In development, `ng serve` uses `proxy.conf.json` pointing to nginx (`http://localhost:8080`), not to Strapi, so the same allowlist is tested.
- There is no persistent content cache: no `localStorage`, no `sessionStorage`, no service worker (`@angular/service-worker` is not installed). The country configuration is kept in memory for the lifetime of the app load (ADR-0004).
- The simulated payment makes no request (REQ-03.20).

### 5. Content-change ACs: interception (3c) and manual check in G5 (3d)

**Mechanism.** The e2e does not write to Strapi or use any credential. To simulate "the business publishes a change and I reload":

1. Loads the page against the real Strapi with the seed.
2. Registers `page.route` on the affected request. The handler gets the **real response** with `route.fetch()`, applies only the scenario's change to its JSON and returns it with `route.fulfill({ response, body })`.
3. Reloads and checks the UI.

This way only the change is simulated; the rest of the response (v5 format, `documentId`, components) is Strapi's.

| AC | Change applied by the interception |
|---|---|
| AC-01.3 | C4: adds a new published field |
| AC-01.10 | C4: removes field A and swaps the `order` of B and C |
| AC-01.11 | No interception: the **seed includes one draft field per country** (content-model §6), and the e2e checks against the real Strapi that it does not appear and that no app request carries `status` or `publicationFilter` |
| AC-01.13 (2nd part) | C4: adds the option "Marca C" to the brand `select` |
| AC-01.31 | C3: changes `formStepTexts.continueLabel` only in the CL response; CO unchanged |
| AC-02.21, AC-03.19 | C5: removes the persisted plan from the list (deactivated or unpublished) or changes its `currency` |
| AC-02.25 | C5 or C6: changes the order, the recommended plan, a plan's base price, or a `priceFactors` band |
| AC-03.15 | C7: changes CL's `termsAndConditions` |

Interception also covers the cases Strapi does not allow publishing, and failures: missing required text (AC-01.35, AC-02.33, AC-03.36; G3-5), unknown type or field without a label (AC-01.25), different currency (AC-02.14), plan without a price (AC-02.15), 30 plans (AC-02.32), errors and latency (AC-01.7, AC-01.8, AC-02.23, AC-02.24, AC-03.16, AC-03.17) and terms with HTML (AC-03.14).

**Manual check in G5 (G3-3).** With the stack running, the human:

1. Adds and publishes a new field for a country in the Strapi admin, reloads the app and checks that it appears (AC-01.3).
2. Deactivates a plan, reloads the plans step and checks that it no longer appears (AC-02.25).
3. Reverts both changes.

The result is recorded in `docs/qa/manual-check.md`. The e2e report states that the real Strapi → app integration for those ACs is verified in that check.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Three independent layers:
    - nginx: GET-only, allowlist and no `Authorization`.
    - Permissions: only `find` on four types, and routers with `only: ['find']`.
    - Strapi middleware: published only.
  - An error in one of them does not expose writes or drafts.
  - There is no write credential anywhere in the project: not in `.env`, not in `e2e/`, not in the frontend. The surface of the PDF's security requirement is reduced to zero.
  - All e2e tests run with `docker compose up` and `npx playwright test`, with no prior steps. No AC is left "Not executed" for anyone who clones the repository.
  - The e2e tests do not modify the demo database and can run in parallel.
  - "Reload" always asks Strapi and nothing in between stores responses (Q-01.20).
- **Negative:**
  - The PDF scenarios "Configuration change without deployment" (AC-01.3) and the plans change (AC-02.25) **are not tested automatically against a real change in Strapi**. What is automated proves that the app reflects a different response on reload. That Strapi produces that response after publishing is checked once by hand in G5, and that evidence is not repeated on every run.
  - `route.fetch()` + modification depends on the e2e knowing the JSON shape (api-contracts). If the contract changes, the tests must be updated.
  - Unpublishing from the admin is only checked indirectly (seed drafts and manual check).
  - `no-store` prevents any browser caching for `/api`. At this volume it does not matter, but each reload costs all the requests.
  - `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` weakens the CSP against style injection (it is the documented alternative without a nonce).
  - The `published-only` middleware and `only: ['find']` are custom code in `cms/`: if a new public content type does not reference them, it is exposed. A review checklist item watches for it.
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *`ctx.query` is not yet processed when the route middleware runs* (the documentation does not specify it). It is checked with the confirmation below. If it fails, a global middleware registered in `config/middlewares.ts` after `strapi::query` is used.
  - *Exposure of the Strapi admin:* only on `127.0.0.1`. The admin uses its own session, which is Strapi's intended use and is not part of the public app.

### Confirmation

- With the stack running (`docker compose up`):
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/plans` → `403`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/api/plans/abc` → `404`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:8080/api/plans?status=draft"` → `400`
  - `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans?status=draft"` (directly to Strapi) → only published plans: the seed has one draft per country (REQ-02.33) that must **not** appear. The same with `/api/form-fields?status=draft` and the seed's draft field
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans` → `404` or `405` (route not loaded because of `only: ['find']`)
  - `curl -sI http://localhost:8080/api/countries` → includes `Cache-Control: no-store`
- E2E AC-01.30, AC-02.31 and AC-03.24: no request from the page carries `Authorization`, and all `/api` requests are `GET`.
- G5: `docs/qa/manual-check.md` records the manual check of the new field and of the deactivated plan.
- Review (security checklist):
  - `grep -rniE "authorization|bearer|api[_-]?token" frontend/ e2e/` → only the AC-01.30 assertion in `e2e/` (it checks the *absence* of the header).
  - `.env.example` contains no Strapi token variable.
  - The bootstrap's public permissions match the table.
  - Each public router has `only: ['find']` and references `global::published-only`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1a. nginx same origin (chosen, D4)

- For: no CORS; a single controllable public surface; sanitizes headers; serves the SPA and the API from the same origin.
- Against: allowlist duplicated with respect to the permissions (two places to maintain).

### 1b. Browser directly to Strapi

- For: one component fewer.
- Against: exposes all Strapi routes (admin included) to the browser, requires CORS and does not allow restricting methods or headers; contradicts D4.

### 1c. BFF

- For: could hide Strapi completely and validate parameters.
- Against: more code and more infrastructure; D4 explicitly excludes it.

### 2a. `published-only` middleware in Strapi (chosen) + best-effort nginx

- For: acts on the query already parsed by Strapi, not on the raw string; does not depend on third parties.
- Against: custom code that has to be referenced in every public router.

### 2b. nginx only

- For: zero code in Strapi.
- Against: it is bypassed by encoding the parameter key, and it does not protect direct access to `127.0.0.1:1337`.

### 2c. No Draft & Publish

- For: removes the problem at the root.
- Against: **it violates** the PDF ("only published and active plans") and AC-01.11 and AC-02.5, which require drafts.

### 2d. Third-party plugin

- For: solves the case with one option.
- Against: a new third-party dependency for a security rule, maintained outside Strapi; the equivalent middleware is short.

### 3a. Real writes with a Custom token (discarded in G3-3)

- For: automatically tests the real Strapi → app integration with the documented Content API. The token would have minimal scope, would never touch the browser and could be revoked.
- Against (reason for discarding it):
  - Strapi does not document how to create tokens in code, so it would have to be created **by hand** in the admin. That is a manual step that clashes with the single-command startup the PDF requires.
  - For anyone who clones the repository without that token, **5 ACs would be left "Not executed"** (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.31 and AC-02.25).
  - In addition, it would add a write credential to the project, tests that mutate the demo database, serial execution with restoration, and unpublishing simulated with deletions.

### 3b. Automated admin login

- For: fully automatic; it would allow truly unpublishing with the Content Manager.
- Against: depends on **undocumented internal endpoints** of the admin, which may change between minor versions. It would require super administrator credentials in the test environment, with far more scope than any token. The official alternatives (admin tokens) are also created by hand.

### 3c. Interception only (chosen, G3-3)

- For: no credentials or manual steps; deterministic and fast; reproducible by anyone who clones the repository; with `route.fetch()` only the change is simulated and the rest of the response is the real one.
- Against: it does not automatically test that Strapi produces the response after publishing. It is compensated by 3d in G5.

### 3d. Manual verification (complement to 3c, G5)

- For: checks the real integration with the admin, including publishing and deactivating.
- Against: it is not repeatable on every run; the evidence is a manual record.

## References

Consulted on 2026-11-22:

- Strapi 5, REST API (endpoints, `POST`/`PUT`, `?status=draft`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest
- Strapi 5, `status` parameter (default `published`, applies to populated relations): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status
- Strapi 5, Draft & Publish (`status` in the Content API, `publicationFilter`, unpublishing in the admin): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/draft-and-publish
- Strapi, open request "Prevent users from querying draft content via REST/GraphQL (via status filter)" (2026-02-03): https://feedback.strapi.io/feature-requests/p/prevent-users-from-querying-draft-content-via-rest-graphql-via-status-filter
- Strapi 5, routes (`createCoreRouter`, `only`, `except`, `config.find.middlewares`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/routes
- Strapi 5, middlewares (location, signature, `global::`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/middlewares
- Strapi 5, pagination (`pageSize` capped by `api.rest.maxLimit`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/sort-pagination
- Strapi 5, API tokens (created in the admin; no documented creation in code): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/api-tokens
- Strapi 5, admin tokens (also created in the admin): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/admin-tokens
- Strapi 5, Users & Permissions (public role, "Enable sign-ups"): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/users-permissions
- nginx, `limit_except` (GET implies HEAD): https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#limit_except

- **Caching:**
  - On `/api/*`: `proxy_hide_header Cache-Control; proxy_hide_header Expires; add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;` and no `proxy_cache`.
  - `index.html`: `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
  - Build bundles with a hash: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  - Since `add_header` is only inherited if the current level defines none (nginx documentation), the security headers are repeated in every `location` that defines `add_header`.
- **SPA security headers:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is the fallback Angular documents for static hosts without a per-request nonce (Angular inserts component `<style>` elements). If the build inserts inline scripts or handlers (e.g. the critical CSS `onload`), `autoCsp` is enabled or critical CSS inlining is disabled; the Angular Developer decides this when verifying the CSP in the browser.

### 3. Strapi: published-only reads in the Content API (2a)

- Route middleware `global::published-only` (`cms/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`), referenced in `config.find.middlewares` of the `createCoreRouter` of the four public types. Before calling `next()`, it replaces `ctx.query.status` with `'published'` and removes `ctx.query.publicationFilter`. It applies to all `find` requests of those types.
- Since no client writes through the Content API (neither the app nor the e2e tests, see §5), the four routers are declared with **`only: ['find']`**. The Content API `findOne`, `create`, `update` and `delete` routes are not loaded. The Strapi admin is not affected, because it uses its own API, not these routes.
- REST API configuration (`cms/config/api.ts`): explicit `defaultLimit: 25`, `maxLimit: 100`, so that the contract's pagination (pageSize 100) is predictable.

### 4. Angular

- `CmsClient` uses relative URLs (`/api/...`) and `HttpClient` without authentication interceptors. **There is no variable, constant or `environment` with credentials.**
- In development, `ng serve` uses `proxy.conf.json` pointing to nginx (`http://localhost:8080`), not to Strapi, so the same allowlist is tested.
- There is no persistent content cache: no `localStorage`, no `sessionStorage`, no service worker (`@angular/service-worker` is not installed). The country configuration is kept in memory for the lifetime of the app load (ADR-0004).
- The simulated payment makes no request (REQ-03.20).

### 5. Content-change ACs: interception (3c) and manual check in G5 (3d)

**Mechanism.** The e2e does not write to Strapi or use any credential. To simulate "the business publishes a change and I reload":

1. Loads the page against the real Strapi with the seed.
2. Registers `page.route` on the affected request. The handler gets the **real response** with `route.fetch()`, applies only the scenario's change to its JSON and returns it with `route.fulfill({ response, body })`.
3. Reloads and checks the UI.

This way only the change is simulated; the rest of the response (v5 format, `documentId`, components) is Strapi's.

| AC | Change applied by the interception |
|---|---|
| AC-01.3 | C4: adds a new published field |
| AC-01.10 | C4: removes field A and swaps the `order` of B and C |
| AC-01.11 | No interception: the **seed includes one draft field per country** (content-model §6), and the e2e checks against the real Strapi that it does not appear and that no app request carries `status` or `publicationFilter` |
| AC-01.13 (2nd part) | C4: adds the option "Marca C" to the brand `select` |
| AC-01.31 | C3: changes `formStepTexts.continueLabel` only in the CL response; CO unchanged |
| AC-02.21, AC-03.19 | C5: removes the persisted plan from the list (deactivated or unpublished) or changes its `currency` |
| AC-02.25 | C5 or C6: changes the order, the recommended plan, a plan's base price, or a `priceFactors` band |
| AC-03.15 | C7: changes CL's `termsAndConditions` |

Interception also covers the cases Strapi does not allow publishing, and failures: missing required text (AC-01.35, AC-02.33, AC-03.36; G3-5), unknown type or field without a label (AC-01.25), different currency (AC-02.14), plan without a price (AC-02.15), 30 plans (AC-02.32), errors and latency (AC-01.7, AC-01.8, AC-02.23, AC-02.24, AC-03.16, AC-03.17) and terms with HTML (AC-03.14).

**Manual check in G5 (G3-3).** With the stack running, the human:

1. Adds and publishes a new field for a country in the Strapi admin, reloads the app and checks that it appears (AC-01.3).
2. Deactivates a plan, reloads the plans step and checks that it no longer appears (AC-02.25).
3. Reverts both changes.

The result is recorded in `docs/qa/manual-check.md`. The e2e report states that the real Strapi → app integration for those ACs is verified in that check.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Three independent layers:
    - nginx: GET-only, allowlist and no `Authorization`.
    - Permissions: only `find` on four types, and routers with `only: ['find']`.
    - Strapi middleware: published only.
  - An error in one of them does not expose writes or drafts.
  - There is no write credential anywhere in the project: not in `.env`, not in `e2e/`, not in the frontend. The surface of the PDF's security requirement is reduced to zero.
  - All e2e tests run with `docker compose up` and `npx playwright test`, with no prior steps. No AC is left "Not executed" for anyone who clones the repository.
  - The e2e tests do not modify the demo database and can run in parallel.
  - "Reload" always asks Strapi and nothing in between stores responses (Q-01.20).
- **Negative:**
  - The PDF scenarios "Configuration change without deployment" (AC-01.3) and the plans change (AC-02.25) **are not tested automatically against a real change in Strapi**. What is automated proves that the app reflects a different response on reload. That Strapi produces that response after publishing is checked once by hand in G5, and that evidence is not repeated on every run.
  - `route.fetch()` + modification depends on the e2e knowing the JSON shape (api-contracts). If the contract changes, the tests must be updated.
  - Unpublishing from the admin is only checked indirectly (seed drafts and manual check).
  - `no-store` prevents any browser caching for `/api`. At this volume it does not matter, but each reload costs all the requests.
  - `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` weakens the CSP against style injection (it is the documented alternative without a nonce).
  - The `published-only` middleware and `only: ['find']` are custom code in `cms/`: if a new public content type does not reference them, it is exposed. A review checklist item watches for it.
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *`ctx.query` is not yet processed when the route middleware runs* (the documentation does not specify it). It is checked with the confirmation below. If it fails, a global middleware registered in `config/middlewares.ts` after `strapi::query` is used.
  - *Exposure of the Strapi admin:* only on `127.0.0.1`. The admin uses its own session, which is Strapi's intended use and is not part of the public app.

### Confirmation

- With the stack running (`docker compose up`):
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/plans` → `403`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/api/plans/abc` → `404`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:8080/api/plans?status=draft"` → `400`
  - `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans?status=draft"` (directly to Strapi) → only published plans: the seed has one draft per country (REQ-02.33) that must **not** appear. The same with `/api/form-fields?status=draft` and the seed's draft field
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans` → `404` or `405` (route not loaded because of `only: ['find']`)
  - `curl -sI http://localhost:8080/api/countries` → includes `Cache-Control: no-store`
- E2E AC-01.30, AC-02.31 and AC-03.24: no request from the page carries `Authorization`, and all `/api` requests are `GET`.
- G5: `docs/qa/manual-check.md` records the manual check of the new field and of the deactivated plan.
- Review (security checklist):
  - `grep -rniE "authorization|bearer|api[_-]?token" frontend/ e2e/` → only the AC-01.30 assertion in `e2e/` (it checks the *absence* of the header).
  - `.env.example` contains no Strapi token variable.
  - The bootstrap's public permissions match the table.
  - Each public router has `only: ['find']` and references `global::published-only`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1a. nginx same origin (chosen, D4)

- For: no CORS; a single controllable public surface; sanitizes headers; serves the SPA and the API from the same origin.
- Against: allowlist duplicated with respect to the permissions (two places to maintain).

### 1b. Browser directly to Strapi

- For: one component fewer.
- Against: exposes all Strapi routes (admin included) to the browser, requires CORS and does not allow restricting methods or headers; contradicts D4.

### 1c. BFF

- For: could hide Strapi completely and validate parameters.
- Against: more code and more infrastructure; D4 explicitly excludes it.

### 2a. `published-only` middleware in Strapi (chosen) + best-effort nginx

- For: acts on the query already parsed by Strapi, not on the raw string; does not depend on third parties.
- Against: custom code that has to be referenced in every public router.

### 2b. nginx only

- For: zero code in Strapi.
- Against: it is bypassed by encoding the parameter key, and it does not protect direct access to `127.0.0.1:1337`.

### 2c. No Draft & Publish

- For: removes the problem at the root.
- Against: **it violates** the PDF ("only published and active plans") and AC-01.11 and AC-02.5, which require drafts.

### 2d. Third-party plugin

- For: solves the case with one option.
- Against: a new third-party dependency for a security rule, maintained outside Strapi; the equivalent middleware is short.

### 3a. Real writes with a Custom token (discarded in G3-3)

- For: automatically tests the real Strapi → app integration with the documented Content API. The token would have minimal scope, would never touch the browser and could be revoked.
- Against (reason for discarding it):
  - Strapi does not document how to create tokens in code, so it would have to be created **by hand** in the admin. That is a manual step that clashes with the single-command startup the PDF requires.
  - For anyone who clones the repository without that token, **5 ACs would be left "Not executed"** (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.31 and AC-02.25).
  - In addition, it would add a write credential to the project, tests that mutate the demo database, serial execution with restoration, and unpublishing simulated with deletions.

### 3b. Automated admin login

- For: fully automatic; it would allow truly unpublishing with the Content Manager.
- Against: depends on **undocumented internal endpoints** of the admin, which may change between minor versions. It would require super administrator credentials in the test environment, with far more scope than any token. The official alternatives (admin tokens) are also created by hand.

### 3c. Interception only (chosen, G3-3)

- For: no credentials or manual steps; deterministic and fast; reproducible by anyone who clones the repository; with `route.fetch()` only the change is simulated and the rest of the response is the real one.
- Against: it does not automatically test that Strapi produces the response after publishing. It is compensated by 3d in G5.

### 3d. Manual verification (complement to 3c, G5)

- For: checks the real integration with the admin, including publishing and deactivating.
- Against: it is not repeatable on every run; the evidence is a manual record.
