10	
11	## Contexto y problema
12	
13	El wizard tiene 3 pasos más una confirmación (D7) y persiste en `sessionStorage` separado por país (D6). Las specs fijan reglas que se cruzan entre las tres historias:
14	
15	- Solo se guardan valores; `isComplete` se calcula cada vez con la configuración vigente y nunca se persiste (G2-10, F-00.5).
16	- Del plan solo se persiste su `documentId`, y el precio se recalcula (G2-9).
17	- La aceptación de términos, el resultado elegido y el estado de pago no se persisten (US-03 §6.2).
18	- Tras un pago exitoso se borra el estado del país y queda una confirmación mínima sin datos personales (REQ-03.28).
19	- La configuración del país se pide una vez por carga de la app (Q-01.20). Los planes y factores, en cada entrada al paso 2 (REQ-02.23) y al resumen (REQ-03.5, REQ-03.14).
20	
21	Hay que decidir el formato y las claves de almacenamiento, dónde vive el estado, cómo se cargan los datos con estados explícitos, cómo funcionan las guardas y cómo se protege el pago.
22	
23	## Factores de decisión
24	
25	- Estado con `signal`/`computed`, zoneless, sin NgModules (D2, `CLAUDE.md` §8).
26	- Lógica en funciones puras (reconciliación, `isComplete`, precio, enmascarado, número de cotización).
27	- Separación estricta por país (REQ-01.25, REQ-03.37).
28	- Tolerancia a datos corruptos o manipulados (US-01 5.4).
29	- Estados de carga, error y vacío en cada llamada, con "cargando" anunciado (REQ-01.3, REQ-02.20, REQ-03.31).
30	- Sin dependencias nuevas.
31	
32	## Opciones consideradas
33	
34	**Formato de persistencia**
35	
36	1. **P1. Una clave por país y por tipo de dato** (`ciq.v1.{cc}.step1`, `.plan`, `.confirmation`), JSON validado al leer.
37	2. **P2. Un único objeto por país** (`ciq.{cc}` con `step1`, `plan`, `confirmation`).
38	3. **P3. Librería de estado con persistencia** (p. ej. `@ngrx/signals` con un plugin de almacenamiento).
39	
40	**Carga de datos**
41	
42	1. **L1. `resource()` de Angular** (estable desde v22) con un *loader* que llama a `CmsClient` (`HttpClient`), que pagina y mapea.
43	2. **L2. `httpResource()`** (estable desde v22) directamente sobre cada URL.
44	3. **L3. `HttpClient` + señales de estado escritas a mano.**
45	
46	**Guardas de navegación**
47	
48	1. **G1. Guards funcionales `canActivate`** que esperan la configuración del país (en memoria) y devuelven `RedirectCommand`, más un indicador "cargando" mientras la navegación está pendiente.
49	2. **G2. Comprobación dentro de cada página**, que redirige con `router.navigate(..., { replaceUrl: true })` tras cargar.
50	
51	## Decisión
52	
53	Opción elegida: **P1 + L1 + G1** (con la comprobación de G2 como respaldo tras un reintento).
54	
55	### Persistencia (P1)
56	
57	Acceso a través de `WizardStorage` (`frontend/src/app/core/storage/`), que recibe el `Storage` por un token `WIZARD_STORAGE` (por defecto `sessionStorage`, sustituible en los tests).
58	
59	| Clave | Contenido (JSON) | Dueño | Se borra |
60	|---|---|---|---|
61	| `ciq.v1.{cc}.step1` | `{ "values": { "<fieldKey>": string \| number \| boolean \| null } }` | US-01 | Tras un pago exitoso |
62	| `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` | `{ "planDocumentId": "<documentId>" }` | US-02 | Tras un pago exitoso; al descartar un plan no disponible (REQ-02.17) |
63	| `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` | `{ "quoteNumber": "CO-20261122-7K3F9Q", "planName": "...", "finalPrice": 1320000, "currency": "COP", "paidAt": "2026-11-22T15:04:05.000Z" }` | US-03 | Con "nueva cotización" |
64	
65	- `{cc}` es el código del país en minúsculas de la URL ya validado. `v1` es la versión del esquema: si cambia, se usa `v2` y las claves `v1` se ignoran y se eliminan.
66	- **No se guarda nada más:** ni configuración, ni planes, ni precios, ni factores, ni términos, ni `isComplete`, ni la aceptación de términos, ni el resultado del pago (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23, G2-9, G2-10, REQ-03.12).
67	- **Lectura defensiva:** si el JSON no se puede interpretar o no tiene la forma esperada, se descarta esa clave y se avisa en consola sin datos personales (5.4). Un valor de tipo inesperado se descarta individualmente.
68	- **Escritura del paso 1:** un `effect()` en `DynamicForm` escribe en cada cambio del modelo los valores **normalizados**: `text` recortado, `NaN` → `null`, `date` como `YYYY-MM-DD` (REQ-01.23, Q-01.16). `action` vuelve a escribir al continuar. Mientras se escribe, el modelo conserva el texto sin recortar, y al salir del campo se sustituye por el recortado.
69	- El documento y la fecha de nacimiento quedan en claro en `sessionStorage` (Q-01.15, Q-03.23); se documenta en el README.
70	
71	### Estado en memoria
72	
73	- `CountryConfigStore` (`providedIn: 'root'`) mantiene un `Map<cc, ResourceRef<CountryConfig>>`. `CountryConfig` = país + textos + `FormConfig`. Se crea al entrar en el país y **no se vuelve a pedir** al navegar entre pasos, solo al recargar o al pulsar "reintentar" (Q-01.20).
74	- `Step1State` deriva del almacenamiento y de la configuración:
75	  - `reconcileStep1(config, stored) → Step1Model`: función pura con la tabla 5.4.
76	  - `evaluateStep1(config, values, { today, minimumAge }) → Step1Result`: función pura. Para cada campo vigente devuelve `key`, `type`, `section`, `role`, `value`, `displayValue` (etiqueta de la opción en `select`) y `valid`, más `isComplete` (REQ-01.27). `isComplete` es `false` si la configuración no está `ready` (vacía, no disponible o con error).
77	  - `isComplete` es un `computed` sobre esas funciones: se recalcula al leerlo y nunca se escribe.
78	- Los planes y factores se piden con `resource()` creado por la página (paso 2 y resumen), así que se cancelan al salir y se vuelven a pedir en cada entrada (REQ-02.23).
79	- Los términos, con su propio `resource()` en el resumen, para mostrar la carga y el error en esa sección (REQ-03.31, REQ-03.32, AC-03.17).
80	
81	### Carga de datos (L1) y estados
82	
83	- `CmsClient` (`core/cms/`) hace la petición `GET`, aplica un **timeout de 10 000 ms** (REQ-02.21 deja el valor al ADR), recorre las páginas si `pageCount > 1` (REQ-02.24), valida la forma global y entrega DTOs. Los mappers convierten los DTOs en dominio (api-contracts).
84	- `resource()` expone el estado de carga, el error y el valor, y permite recargar. Las páginas derivan un único `viewState`: `loading` | `error` | `configError` (falta un texto, G2-2) | `empty` | `unavailable` (G2-5) | `ready`.
85	  - `loading` → "cargando" con `role="status"`.
86	  - `error` → "error de carga" + "reintentar" con `role="alert"`.
87	  - `configError` → mensaje genérico del país o, si también falta, "error de carga" (F-00.7).
88	- Sin reintentos automáticos: solo el botón "reintentar" (REQ-01.4).
89	- Los 4 textos fijos (G2-2) están en un único archivo, `core/ui-state/fixed-texts.ts`.
90	
91	### Navegación y guardas (G1)
92	
93	| Ruta | Guard | Regla | Redirección |
94	|---|---|---|---|
95	| `/:country` (shell) | `countryCaseGuard` | Segmento en mayúsculas | Misma URL en minúsculas (ADR-0001) |
96	| `/:country/plans` | `step1CompleteGuard` | Espera `CountryConfig`. Si está `ready` y `isComplete` es falso | `/:country/form`, sin pedir planes (REQ-02.19, AC-02.22) |
97	| `/:country/summary` | `step1CompleteGuard`, `planSelectedGuard` | `isComplete` falso → paso 1; sin `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` → paso 2 | REQ-03.13, AC-03.18 |
98	| `/:country/confirmation` | `confirmationGuard` | Sin `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` válido | `/:country/form` (REQ-03.29) |
99	
100	- Los guards devuelven `true` si la configuración **falla** al cargar. La página muestra entonces "error de carga" y, tras un "reintentar" con éxito, vuelve a evaluar `isComplete` y redirige si hace falta (respaldo G2).
101	- Mientras un guard espera, el componente raíz muestra "cargando" (señal derivada de los eventos del `Router`: `NavigationStart` → `true`; `NavigationEnd`, `NavigationCancel` o `NavigationError` → `false`). Así se cumple REQ-02.20 cuando se entra por URL.
102	- **Plan no disponible en el resumen** (REQ-03.14, G2-11): el resumen carga los planes y, si el plan persistido no está en la lista vigente, navega a `/:country/plans` sin borrar nada. El paso 2 detecta el mismo caso, descarta la selección y muestra el aviso (REQ-02.17). Así hay una única implementación del descarte.
103	- **Desde el resumen** (REQ-03.9 a REQ-03.11): "editar datos" → `/form`; desde ahí continuar → `/plans` con el plan preseleccionado → `/summary`.
104	- **Foco al cambiar de paso** (REQ-01.31, REQ-02.28, REQ-03.33): cada página enfoca su `<h1 tabindex="-1">` con `afterNextRender`, y el shell actualiza `document.title` con el título del paso (texto de Strapi).
105	
106	### Pago simulado y confirmación (D9, G2-12)
107	
108	- Estado local de `SummaryStepPage`, sin persistir:
109	  - `termsAccepted = signal(false)`
110	  - `outcome = signal<'approved' | 'rejected'>('approved')`
111	  - `payment = signal<'idle' | 'processing' | 'rejected'>('idle')`
112	- `canPay = computed(...)` con los datos cargados y válidos, el plan válido, los términos cargados y aceptados, y `payment() !== 'processing'` (REQ-03.19).
113	- `pay()` sale de inmediato si `payment() === 'processing'`. Es la **guarda en el estado**, independiente del atributo `disabled` (REQ-03.23). Después cambia el estado a `processing` y llama a `MockPaymentGateway.pay(outcome, abortSignal)`, que resuelve tras `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS` (token, 1500 ms por defecto; REQ-03.24). No hace ninguna petición (REQ-03.20).
114	- Al destruir la página se aborta el pago pendiente (`DestroyRef`) y su resultado se ignora (REQ-03.22).
115	- **Éxito**, en este orden:
116	  1. Genera el número con `createQuoteNumber(cc, now, randomSource)`, una función pura con `crypto.getRandomValues` inyectado (REQ-03.26).
117	  2. Escribe `confirmation`.
118	  3. Borra `step1` y `plan`.
119	  4. Navega a `/:country/confirmation` con `replaceUrl: true`.
120	
121	  Si se vuelve atrás después, el resumen redirige al paso 1 vacío porque `isComplete` es falso (REQ-03.28, AC-03.29).
122	- **Rechazo:** `payment.set('rejected')`, mensaje con `role="alert"`; se conservan los datos y la aceptación de términos (REQ-03.30).
123	- **Nueva cotización:** borra `confirmation` y navega a `/:country/form`.
124	
125	## Consecuencias
126	
127	- **Positivas:**
128	  - Cada clave tiene un único dueño y un ciclo de vida claro. Si una clave está corrupta, solo se pierde esa (p. ej., el paso 1), como pide 5.4.
129	  - `isComplete` no puede quedar obsoleto porque no existe en el almacenamiento (F-00.5).
130	  - `resource()` aporta la cancelación por `AbortSignal` al salir de la página o al recargar, y un estado uniforme para carga, error y reintento.
131	  - Las redirecciones ocurren antes de pintar el paso y antes de pedir planes (AC-02.22).
132	- **Negativas:**
133	  - Tres claves por país: el borrado tras el pago son dos operaciones, sin atomicidad. Si la pestaña muere entre las dos, puede quedar un `plan` huérfano, que es inofensivo porque sin `step1` el resumen redirige al paso 1.
134	  - El documento queda en claro en `sessionStorage` mientras dura la cotización (riesgo aceptado en G2).
135	  - Los guards esperan una petición HTTP: la primera navegación por URL directa a `/plans` o `/summary` muestra el "cargando" global antes que el del paso.
136	  - Hay dos lugares que evalúan `isComplete` (guard y página tras un reintento); se mitiga usando la misma función pura.
137	  - No se impide pagar en una pestaña duplicada (limitación aceptada, REQ-03.23).
138	- **Riesgos y mitigación:**
139	  - *Nombres exactos de las señales de `ResourceRef`:* la guía de `httpResource` documenta `value()`, `hasValue()`, `error()` e `isLoading()`. El Angular Developer confirma en la referencia de `ResourceRef` el método de recarga antes de implementarlo.
140	  - *El `effect()` de escritura se ejecuta con el modelo inicial y sobrescribe lo guardado antes de reconciliar:* el modelo se inicializa con los valores ya reconciliados, así que la primera escritura es idempotente. Hay un unit test que lo verifica (AC-01.21).
141	
142	### Confirmación
143	
144	- Unit: `reconcileStep1` (AC-01.23, AC-01.24), `evaluateStep1` (AC-01.29), `WizardStorage` (JSON corrupto, tipos inesperados, separación por país: AC-01.22), guards (AC-02.22, AC-03.18, AC-03.30), `SummaryStepPage` con `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS = 0` y contador de intentos (AC-03.22, AC-03.23), `createQuoteNumber` (AC-03.27).
145	- E2E: AC-01.4, AC-01.21, AC-02.19, AC-02.20, AC-02.30, AC-03.10, AC-03.11, AC-03.28, AC-03.29.
146	- Review: `grep -rn "localStorage\|serviceWorker\|isComplete.*setItem" frontend/src` sin resultados; las únicas llamadas a `sessionStorage` están en `core/storage/`.
147	
148	## Pros y contras de las opciones
149	
150	### P1. Una clave por país y por dato (elegida)
151	
152	- A favor: corrupción aislada; dueño claro por historia; fácil de inspeccionar en los e2e (AC-01.29: "no completed flag stored").
153	- En contra: varias escrituras al limpiar; más claves.
154	
155	### P2. Un objeto por país
156	
157	- A favor: una sola escritura y un borrado atómico.
158	- En contra: si el JSON se corrompe se pierde todo el país, no solo el paso 1 (la tabla 5.4 dice "todo lo del paso 1"). Cada historia reescribe el objeto completo, lo que acopla a las tres.
159	
160	### P3. Librería de estado con persistencia
161	
162	- A favor: patrones ya hechos (hidratación, selectores).
163	- En contra: dependencia nueva sin necesidad real (`CLAUDE.md` §6); el estado es pequeño.
164	
165	### L1. `resource()` + `CmsClient` (elegida)
166	
167	- A favor: estable en v22; el *loader* asíncrono permite paginar y mapear en un solo paso; cancela al destruirse.
168	- En contra: añade un nivel de indirección respecto a `httpResource`.
169	
170	### L2. `httpResource()`
171	
172	- A favor: muy conciso; usa `HttpClient` (con interceptores); opción `parse` para validar.
173	- En contra: una URL por recurso. Recorrer las páginas (REQ-02.24) y combinar las peticiones de configuración (país + campos) exige componer varios recursos a mano.
174	
175	### L3. `HttpClient` + señales manuales
176	
177	- A favor: control total y API muy conocida.
178	- En contra: reimplementa cancelación, estado y recarga en cada página, con más superficie para errores en los estados de carga.
179	
180	### G1. Guards funcionales (elegida)
181	
182	- A favor: la redirección ocurre antes de activar el componente, así que no se piden planes (AC-02.22). Es el mecanismo idiomático de Angular.
183	- En contra: hace falta un indicador global de navegación pendiente; un guard que falla al cargar debe dejar pasar la navegación.
184	
185	### G2. Comprobación en la página
186	
187	- A favor: el estado de carga es local y natural.
188	- En contra: el componente llega a activarse y podría pedir planes antes de decidir; la lógica de acceso queda repartida entre páginas.
189	
190	## Referencias
191	
192	Consultadas el 2026-11-22:
193	
194	- Angular, `resource()` (estable desde v22.0, cancelación con `AbortSignal`): https://angular.dev/api/core/resource
195	- Angular, `httpResource` (estable desde v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/common/http/httpResource

# ADR-0003 — Strapi access, security, caching and content changes in the e2e tests

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
| Date | 2026-11-22 |
| Author | Software Architect (subagent) |
| Deciders | Human (G3) |
| Motivated by | D4, D9 · G2-13 (Q-01.20) · G3-2, G3-3 · REQ-01.6, REQ-01.35, REQ-02.2, REQ-02.23, REQ-02.31, REQ-03.20, REQ-03.24 · AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.13, AC-01.30, AC-01.31, AC-02.21, AC-02.25, AC-02.31, AC-03.15, AC-03.19, AC-03.24 |

## Context and problem

The PDF requires that "no Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser" and "public role permissions minimal and justified". D4 (G0) set the following: public role with only `find`/`findOne`, nginx as a GET-only proxy with an allowlist, no token in the browser and no BFF. Four things remain to be specified:

1. The exact permissions and the allowlist.
2. That "reload" always shows what is published: no intermediate cache (Q-01.20, REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23).
3. That drafts are never served (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.2).
4. How to test the ACs that describe a content change in Strapi (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.13, AC-01.31, AC-02.21, AC-02.25, AC-03.15, AC-03.19) without breaking the single-command startup or introducing credentials.

### Finding: the public role can read drafts

In Strapi 5, the REST API `status` parameter accepts `draft` and `published`, and the default value is `published`. **There is no separate permission for reading drafts.** According to the open request on the Strapi feedback portal (February 3, 2026), "any user with find or findOne permission on a content-type can access draft entries by using the status parameter". The Draft & Publish documentation confirms that the Content API can request "draft or published content" with `status`, and also mentions the `publicationFilter` parameter. The `status` parameter page does not say which permission `status=draft` requires (orchestrator verification in `reviews/001-G3-architecture-check.md`). That is why the middleware is kept as defense in depth, and its confirmation `curl` is mandatory during implementation.

Consequence: with D4 as it stands, a public `GET /api/plans?status=draft` request could return drafts (unpublished plans or terms). The app never makes it (REQ-01.6), but a visitor could. D4 remains viable, but it needs an additional measure that does not contradict it: forcing `published` on the public routes.

## Decision drivers

- No token in the browser or in the bundle (`CLAUDE.md` §6).
- Minimal public surface: only what US-01, US-02 and US-03 read (api-contracts).
- Defense in depth: a failure in one layer (nginx, Strapi permissions or code) does not expose writes or drafts.
- Changes visible on reload, with no intermediate HTTP cache.
- E2E tests reproducible with `docker compose up` by anyone who clones the repository, without manual steps or credentials (PDF: "a single command to start the whole project").
- No new dependencies.

## Considered options

**Axis 1: how the browser reaches Strapi**

1. **1a. nginx same origin, GET-only with an exact allowlist and header sanitization (D4).**
2. **1b. Browser directly to Strapi (`:1337`) with CORS.**
3. **1c. Custom BFF** (Node) that calls Strapi with server credentials.

**Axis 2: how to avoid drafts in public reads**

1. **2a. Strapi route middleware `published-only`** on the public `find` routes, plus a best-effort rejection in nginx.
2. **2b. nginx only**: reject `status` and `publicationFilter` in the query.
3. **2c. Disable Draft & Publish** on the public content types.
4. **2d. Third-party plugin** (`strapi-plugin-draft-preview`, `guardNativeStatus` option).

**Axis 3: how the content-change ACs are tested** (G3-3)

1. **3a. Real writes to Strapi from the Playwright Node process** with a Custom API token created by hand in the admin.
2. **3b. Automated administrator login** from Playwright and use of the admin's internal endpoints (Content Manager).
3. **3c. Network interception only** (`page.route`): the e2e modifies Strapi's real response in the test browser.
4. **3d. Manual verification** of the real change in Strapi.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1a + 2a + 3c**, with **3d** for the real change in Strapi, which is checked by hand in G5 (G3-3).

### 1. Strapi public role (idempotent bootstrap)

**Only `find`**, without `findOne`, on four types (G3-2: a refinement of D4, which set `find`/`findOne` as the maximum):

| Permission | Reason | Reads that use it |
|---|---|---|
| `api::country.country.find` | Country list (`/`, "país no disponible"), country configuration, factors, terms | C1, C3, C6, C7 (api-contracts) |
| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | The country's step 1 fields | C4 |
| `api::plan.plan.find` | The country's plans | C5 |
| `api::country-selection.country-selection.find` | `/` texts | C2 |

- **`findOne` is not granted** on any type: no read needs it (the chosen plan is checked against the list, REQ-03.14).
- The bootstrap **removes any other permission** from the public role (including those of `plugin::users-permissions.auth.*` and those of `upload`) and disables user registration ("Enable sign-ups" = false) in the Users & Permissions advanced settings. It is idempotent: on every startup it leaves exactly this table.
- No type uses i18n (ADR-0001). The `authenticated` role has no permissions.

### 2. nginx (the browser's only entry point)

- Serves the Angular build and proxies `/api` to Strapi on the internal Docker network. The Strapi port is published only on `127.0.0.1:1337`, for the business admin. The Strapi admin does not go through nginx.
- **Exact allowlist** with `location =`:
  - `/api/countries`
  - `/api/form-fields`
  - `/api/plans`
  - `/api/country-selection`
- `location /api/` → `404` for everything else: `findOne` (`/api/plans/<id>`), `/api/auth/*`, `/api/upload`, `/api/users`...
- In each allowed `location`, `limit_except GET { deny all; }`. According to the nginx documentation, allowing `GET` also allows `HEAD`; any other method receives `403`.
- **Request sanitization:** `proxy_set_header Authorization "";` and `proxy_set_header Cookie "";`. Even if a header arrived from the browser, it is never forwarded.
- **Best-effort draft rejection:** `if ($args ~* "(^|&)(status|publicationFilter)(=|%5B|\[)") { return 400; }`. It is *best-effort* because `$args` is the undecoded query and an encoded key (`%73tatus`) would bypass it. The real guarantee is the Strapi middleware.
- **Caching:**
  - On `/api/*`: `proxy_hide_header Cache-Control; proxy_hide_header Expires; add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;` and no `proxy_cache`.
  - `index.html`: `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
  - Build bundles with a hash: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  - Since `add_header` is only inherited if the current level defines none (nginx documentation), the security headers are repeated in every `location` that defines `add_header`.
- **SPA security headers:** `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is the fallback Angular documents for static hosts without a per-request nonce (Angular inserts component `<style>` elements). If the build inserts inline scripts or handlers (e.g. the critical CSS `onload`), `autoCsp` is enabled or critical CSS inlining is disabled; the Angular Developer decides this when verifying the CSP in the browser.

### 3. Strapi: published-only reads in the Content API (2a)

- Route middleware `global::published-only` (`cms/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`), referenced in `config.find.middlewares` of the `createCoreRouter` of the four public types. Before calling `next()`, it replaces `ctx.query.status` with `'published'` and removes `ctx.query.publicationFilter`. It applies to all `find` requests of those types.
- Since no client writes through the Content API (neither the app nor the e2e tests, see §5), the four routers are declared with **`only: ['find']`**. The Content API `findOne`, `create`, `update` and `delete` routes are not loaded. The Strapi admin is not affected, because it uses its own API, not these routes.
- REST API configuration (`cms/config/api.ts`): explicit `defaultLimit: 25`, `maxLimit: 100`, so that the contract's pagination (pageSize 100) is predictable.

### 4. Angular

- `CmsClient` uses relative URLs (`/api/...`) and `HttpClient` without authentication interceptors. **There is no variable, constant or `environment` with credentials.**
- In development, `ng serve` uses `proxy.conf.json` pointing to nginx (`http://localhost:8080`), not to Strapi, so the same allowlist is tested.
- There is no persistent content cache: no `localStorage`, no `sessionStorage`, no service worker (`@angular/service-worker` is not installed). The country configuration is kept in memory for the lifetime of the app load (ADR-0004).
- The simulated payment makes no request (REQ-03.20).

### 5. Content-change ACs: interception (3c) and manual check in G5 (3d)

**Mechanism.** The e2e does not write to Strapi or use any credential. To simulate "the business publishes a change and I reload":

1. Loads the page against the real Strapi with the seed.
2. Registers `page.route` on the affected request. The handler gets the **real response** with `route.fetch()`, applies only the scenario's change to its JSON and returns it with `route.fulfill({ response, body })`.
3. Reloads and checks the UI.

This way only the change is simulated; the rest of the response (v5 format, `documentId`, components) is Strapi's.

| AC | Change applied by the interception |
|---|---|
| AC-01.3 | C4: adds a new published field |
| AC-01.10 | C4: removes field A and swaps the `order` of B and C |
| AC-01.11 | No interception: the **seed includes one draft field per country** (content-model §6), and the e2e checks against the real Strapi that it does not appear and that no app request carries `status` or `publicationFilter` |
| AC-01.13 (2nd part) | C4: adds the option "Marca C" to the brand `select` |
| AC-01.31 | C3: changes `formStepTexts.continueLabel` only in the CL response; CO unchanged |
| AC-02.21, AC-03.19 | C5: removes the persisted plan from the list (deactivated or unpublished) or changes its `currency` |
| AC-02.25 | C5 or C6: changes the order, the recommended plan, a plan's base price, or a `priceFactors` band |
| AC-03.15 | C7: changes CL's `termsAndConditions` |

Interception also covers the cases Strapi does not allow publishing, and failures: missing required text (AC-01.35, AC-02.33, AC-03.36; G3-5), unknown type or field without a label (AC-01.25), different currency (AC-02.14), plan without a price (AC-02.15), 30 plans (AC-02.32), errors and latency (AC-01.7, AC-01.8, AC-02.23, AC-02.24, AC-03.16, AC-03.17) and terms with HTML (AC-03.14).

**Manual check in G5 (G3-3).** With the stack running, the human:

1. Adds and publishes a new field for a country in the Strapi admin, reloads the app and checks that it appears (AC-01.3).
2. Deactivates a plan, reloads the plans step and checks that it no longer appears (AC-02.25).
3. Reverts both changes.

The result is recorded in `docs/qa/manual-check.md`. The e2e report states that the real Strapi → app integration for those ACs is verified in that check.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Three independent layers:
    - nginx: GET-only, allowlist and no `Authorization`.
    - Permissions: only `find` on four types, and routers with `only: ['find']`.
    - Strapi middleware: published only.
  - An error in one of them does not expose writes or drafts.
  - There is no write credential anywhere in the project: not in `.env`, not in `e2e/`, not in the frontend. The surface of the PDF's security requirement is reduced to zero.
  - All e2e tests run with `docker compose up` and `npx playwright test`, with no prior steps. No AC is left "Not executed" for anyone who clones the repository.
  - The e2e tests do not modify the demo database and can run in parallel.
  - "Reload" always asks Strapi and nothing in between stores responses (Q-01.20).
- **Negative:**
  - The PDF scenarios "Configuration change without deployment" (AC-01.3) and the plans change (AC-02.25) **are not tested automatically against a real change in Strapi**. What is automated proves that the app reflects a different response on reload. That Strapi produces that response after publishing is checked once by hand in G5, and that evidence is not repeated on every run.
  - `route.fetch()` + modification depends on the e2e knowing the JSON shape (api-contracts). If the contract changes, the tests must be updated.
  - Unpublishing from the admin is only checked indirectly (seed drafts and manual check).
  - `no-store` prevents any browser caching for `/api`. At this volume it does not matter, but each reload costs all the requests.
  - `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` weakens the CSP against style injection (it is the documented alternative without a nonce).
  - The `published-only` middleware and `only: ['find']` are custom code in `cms/`: if a new public content type does not reference them, it is exposed. A review checklist item watches for it.
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *`ctx.query` is not yet processed when the route middleware runs* (the documentation does not specify it). It is checked with the confirmation below. If it fails, a global middleware registered in `config/middlewares.ts` after `strapi::query` is used.
  - *Exposure of the Strapi admin:* only on `127.0.0.1`. The admin uses its own session, which is Strapi's intended use and is not part of the public app.

### Confirmation

- With the stack running (`docker compose up`):
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/plans` → `403`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/api/plans/abc` → `404`
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:8080/api/plans?status=draft"` → `400`
  - `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans?status=draft"` (directly to Strapi) → only published plans: the seed has one draft per country (REQ-02.33) that must **not** appear. The same with `/api/form-fields?status=draft` and the seed's draft field
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:1337/api/plans` → `404` or `405` (route not loaded because of `only: ['find']`)
  - `curl -sI http://localhost:8080/api/countries` → includes `Cache-Control: no-store`
- E2E AC-01.30, AC-02.31 and AC-03.24: no request from the page carries `Authorization`, and all `/api` requests are `GET`.
- G5: `docs/qa/manual-check.md` records the manual check of the new field and of the deactivated plan.
- Review (security checklist):
  - `grep -rniE "authorization|bearer|api[_-]?token" frontend/ e2e/` → only the AC-01.30 assertion in `e2e/` (it checks the *absence* of the header).
  - `.env.example` contains no Strapi token variable.
  - The bootstrap's public permissions match the table.
  - Each public router has `only: ['find']` and references `global::published-only`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1a. nginx same origin (chosen, D4)

- For: no CORS; a single controllable public surface; sanitizes headers; serves the SPA and the API from the same origin.
- Against: allowlist duplicated with respect to the permissions (two places to maintain).

### 1b. Browser directly to Strapi

- For: one component fewer.
- Against: exposes all Strapi routes (admin included) to the browser, requires CORS and does not allow restricting methods or headers; contradicts D4.

### 1c. BFF

- For: could hide Strapi completely and validate parameters.
- Against: more code and more infrastructure; D4 explicitly excludes it.

### 2a. `published-only` middleware in Strapi (chosen) + best-effort nginx

- For: acts on the query already parsed by Strapi, not on the raw string; does not depend on third parties.
- Against: custom code that has to be referenced in every public router.

### 2b. nginx only

- For: zero code in Strapi.
- Against: it is bypassed by encoding the parameter key, and it does not protect direct access to `127.0.0.1:1337`.

### 2c. No Draft & Publish

- For: removes the problem at the root.
- Against: **it violates** the PDF ("only published and active plans") and AC-01.11 and AC-02.5, which require drafts.

### 2d. Third-party plugin

- For: solves the case with one option.
- Against: a new third-party dependency for a security rule, maintained outside Strapi; the equivalent middleware is short.

### 3a. Real writes with a Custom token (discarded in G3-3)

- For: automatically tests the real Strapi → app integration with the documented Content API. The token would have minimal scope, would never touch the browser and could be revoked.
- Against (reason for discarding it):
  - Strapi does not document how to create tokens in code, so it would have to be created **by hand** in the admin. That is a manual step that clashes with the single-command startup the PDF requires.
  - For anyone who clones the repository without that token, **5 ACs would be left "Not executed"** (AC-01.3, AC-01.10, AC-01.11, AC-01.31 and AC-02.25).
  - In addition, it would add a write credential to the project, tests that mutate the demo database, serial execution with restoration, and unpublishing simulated with deletions.

### 3b. Automated admin login

- For: fully automatic; it would allow truly unpublishing with the Content Manager.
- Against: depends on **undocumented internal endpoints** of the admin, which may change between minor versions. It would require super administrator credentials in the test environment, with far more scope than any token. The official alternatives (admin tokens) are also created by hand.

### 3c. Interception only (chosen, G3-3)

- For: no credentials or manual steps; deterministic and fast; reproducible by anyone who clones the repository; with `route.fetch()` only the change is simulated and the rest of the response is the real one.
- Against: it does not automatically test that Strapi produces the response after publishing. It is compensated by 3d in G5.

### 3d. Manual verification (complement to 3c, G5)

- For: checks the real integration with the admin, including publishing and deactivating.
- Against: it is not repeatable on every run; the evidence is a manual record.

## References

# ADR-0004 — Wizard state, data loading, persistence and navigation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
| Date | 2026-11-22 |
| Author | Software Architect (subagent) |
| Deciders | Human (G3) |
| Motivated by | D6, D7, D9 · G2-9, G2-10, G2-11, G2-12, G2-13 · REQ-01.3, REQ-01.4, REQ-01.6, REQ-01.18, REQ-01.23 to REQ-01.27, REQ-01.31, REQ-02.16 to REQ-02.23, REQ-02.30, REQ-03.1, REQ-03.5, REQ-03.9 to REQ-03.14, REQ-03.19, REQ-03.21 to REQ-03.32, REQ-03.37 |

## Context and problem

The wizard has 3 steps plus a confirmation (D7) and persists in `sessionStorage`, separated by country (D6). The specs set rules that cut across the three stories:

- Only values are stored; `isComplete` is computed each time with the current configuration and is never persisted (G2-10, F-00.5).
- Only the plan's `documentId` is persisted, and the price is recomputed (G2-9).
- The terms acceptance, the chosen outcome and the payment state are not persisted (US-03 §6.2).
- After a successful payment the country's state is cleared and a minimal confirmation with no personal data remains (REQ-03.28).
- The country configuration is requested once per app load (Q-01.20). Plans and factors, on every entry to step 2 (REQ-02.23) and to the summary (REQ-03.5, REQ-03.14).

We need to decide the storage format and keys, where the state lives, how data is loaded with explicit states, how the guards work and how the payment is protected.

## Decision drivers

- State with `signal`/`computed`, zoneless, no NgModules (D2, `CLAUDE.md` §8).
- Logic in pure functions (reconciliation, `isComplete`, price, masking, quote number).
- Strict separation by country (REQ-01.25, REQ-03.37).
- Tolerance to corrupted or tampered data (US-01 5.4).
- Loading, error and empty states on every call, with "cargando" announced (REQ-01.3, REQ-02.20, REQ-03.31).
- No new dependencies.

## Considered options

**Persistence format**

1. **P1. One key per country and per data type** (`ciq.v1.{cc}.step1`, `.plan`, `.confirmation`), JSON validated on read.
2. **P2. A single object per country** (`ciq.{cc}` with `step1`, `plan`, `confirmation`).
3. **P3. State library with persistence** (e.g. `@ngrx/signals` with a storage plugin).

**Data loading**

1. **L1. Angular `resource()`** (stable since v22) with a *loader* that calls `CmsClient` (`HttpClient`), which paginates and maps.
2. **L2. `httpResource()`** (stable since v22) directly on each URL.
3. **L3. `HttpClient` + hand-written state signals.**

**Navigation guards**

1. **G1. Functional `canActivate` guards** that wait for the country configuration (in memory) and return `RedirectCommand`, plus a "cargando" indicator while navigation is pending.
2. **G2. Check inside each page**, which redirects with `router.navigate(..., { replaceUrl: true })` after loading.

## Decision

Chosen option: **P1 + L1 + G1** (with the G2 check as a fallback after a retry).

### Persistence (P1)

Access through `WizardStorage` (`frontend/src/app/core/storage/`), which receives the `Storage` through a `WIZARD_STORAGE` token (by default `sessionStorage`, replaceable in tests).

| Key | Content (JSON) | Owner | Cleared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.step1` | `{ "values": { "<fieldKey>": string \| number \| boolean \| null } }` | US-01 | After a successful payment |
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` | `{ "planDocumentId": "<documentId>" }` | US-02 | After a successful payment; when discarding an unavailable plan (REQ-02.17) |
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` | `{ "quoteNumber": "CO-20261122-7K3F9Q", "planName": "...", "finalPrice": 1320000, "currency": "COP", "paidAt": "2026-11-22T15:04:05.000Z" }` | US-03 | With "new quote" |

- `{cc}` is the already validated lowercase country code from the URL. `v1` is the schema version: if it changes, `v2` is used and the `v1` keys are ignored and removed.
- **Nothing else is stored:** no configuration, plans, prices, factors, terms, `isComplete`, terms acceptance or payment outcome (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23, G2-9, G2-10, REQ-03.12).
- **Defensive read:** if the JSON cannot be parsed or does not have the expected shape, that key is discarded and a console warning is logged without personal data (5.4). A value of an unexpected type is discarded individually.
- **Step 1 write:** an `effect()` in `DynamicForm` writes the **normalized** values on every model change: trimmed `text`, `NaN` → `null`, `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` (REQ-01.23, Q-01.16). `action` writes again on continue. While typing, the model keeps the untrimmed text, and when leaving the field it is replaced by the trimmed one.
- The document and the birth date remain in plain text in `sessionStorage` (Q-01.15, Q-03.23); this is documented in the README.

### In-memory state

- `CountryConfigStore` (`providedIn: 'root'`) holds a `Map<cc, ResourceRef<CountryConfig>>`. `CountryConfig` = country + texts + `FormConfig`. It is created when entering the country and **is not requested again** when navigating between steps, only on reload or when pressing "reintentar" (Q-01.20).
- `Step1State` derives from the storage and the configuration:
  - `reconcileStep1(config, stored) → Step1Model`: pure function with table 5.4.
  - `evaluateStep1(config, values, { today, minimumAge }) → Step1Result`: pure function. For each current field it returns `key`, `type`, `section`, `role`, `value`, `displayValue` (option label for `select`) and `valid`, plus `isComplete` (REQ-01.27). `isComplete` is `false` if the configuration is not `ready` (empty, unavailable or with an error).
  - `isComplete` is a `computed` over those functions: it is recomputed when read and never written.
- Plans and factors are requested with a `resource()` created by the page (step 2 and summary), so they are cancelled on leaving and requested again on every entry (REQ-02.23).
- The terms, with their own `resource()` in the summary, to show loading and error in that section (REQ-03.31, REQ-03.32, AC-03.17).

### Data loading (L1) and states

- `CmsClient` (`core/cms/`) makes the `GET` request, applies a **10 000 ms timeout** (REQ-02.21 leaves the value to the ADR), walks the pages if `pageCount > 1` (REQ-02.24), validates the overall shape and delivers DTOs. The mappers convert DTOs into domain objects (api-contracts).
- `resource()` exposes the loading state, the error and the value, and allows reloading. The pages derive a single `viewState`: `loading` | `error` | `configError` (a text is missing, G2-2) | `empty` | `unavailable` (G2-5) | `ready`.
  - `loading` → "cargando" with `role="status"`.
  - `error` → "error de carga" + "reintentar" with `role="alert"`.
  - `configError` → the country's generic message or, if that is also missing, "error de carga" (F-00.7).
- No automatic retries: only the "reintentar" button (REQ-01.4).
- The 4 fixed texts (G2-2) are in a single file, `core/ui-state/fixed-texts.ts`.

### Navigation and guards (G1)

| Route | Guard | Rule | Redirect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/:country` (shell) | `countryCaseGuard` | Uppercase segment | Same URL in lowercase (ADR-0001) |
| `/:country/plans` | `step1CompleteGuard` | Waits for `CountryConfig`. If it is `ready` and `isComplete` is false | `/:country/form`, without requesting plans (REQ-02.19, AC-02.22) |
| `/:country/summary` | `step1CompleteGuard`, `planSelectedGuard` | `isComplete` false → step 1; no `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` → step 2 | REQ-03.13, AC-03.18 |
| `/:country/confirmation` | `confirmationGuard` | No valid `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` | `/:country/form` (REQ-03.29) |

- The guards return `true` if the configuration **fails** to load. The page then shows "error de carga" and, after a successful "reintentar", evaluates `isComplete` again and redirects if needed (G2 fallback).
- While a guard is waiting, the root component shows "cargando" (a signal derived from `Router` events: `NavigationStart` → `true`; `NavigationEnd`, `NavigationCancel` or `NavigationError` → `false`). This satisfies REQ-02.20 when entering by URL.
- **Plan not available in the summary** (REQ-03.14, G2-11): the summary loads the plans and, if the persisted plan is not in the current list, navigates to `/:country/plans` without clearing anything. Step 2 detects the same case, discards the selection and shows the notice (REQ-02.17). This way there is a single implementation of the discard.
- **From the summary** (REQ-03.9 to REQ-03.11): "edit data" → `/form`; from there continue → `/plans` with the plan preselected → `/summary`.
- **Focus when changing step** (REQ-01.31, REQ-02.28, REQ-03.33): each page focuses its `<h1 tabindex="-1">` with `afterNextRender`, and the shell updates `document.title` with the step title (Strapi text).

### Simulated payment and confirmation (D9, G2-12)

- Local state of `SummaryStepPage`, not persisted:
  - `termsAccepted = signal(false)`
  - `outcome = signal<'approved' | 'rejected'>('approved')`
  - `payment = signal<'idle' | 'processing' | 'rejected'>('idle')`
- `canPay = computed(...)` with the data loaded and valid, the plan valid, the terms loaded and accepted, and `payment() !== 'processing'` (REQ-03.19).
- `pay()` returns immediately if `payment() === 'processing'`. This is the **guard in the state**, independent of the `disabled` attribute (REQ-03.23). Then it changes the state to `processing` and calls `MockPaymentGateway.pay(outcome, abortSignal)`, which resolves after `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS` (token, 1500 ms by default; REQ-03.24). It makes no request (REQ-03.20).
- When the page is destroyed, the pending payment is aborted (`DestroyRef`) and its result is ignored (REQ-03.22).
- **Success**, in this order:
  1. Generates the number with `createQuoteNumber(cc, now, randomSource)`, a pure function with `crypto.getRandomValues` injected (REQ-03.26).
  2. Writes `confirmation`.
  3. Clears `step1` and `plan`.
  4. Navigates to `/:country/confirmation` with `replaceUrl: true`.

  If the user goes back afterwards, the summary redirects to an empty step 1 because `isComplete` is false (REQ-03.28, AC-03.29).
- **Rejection:** `payment.set('rejected')`, message with `role="alert"`; the data and the terms acceptance are kept (REQ-03.30).
- **New quote:** clears `confirmation` and navigates to `/:country/form`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Each key has a single owner and a clear life cycle. If a key is corrupted, only that one is lost (e.g. step 1), as 5.4 requires.
  - `isComplete` cannot become stale because it does not exist in storage (F-00.5).
  - `resource()` provides cancellation via `AbortSignal` when leaving the page or reloading, and a uniform state for loading, error and retry.
  - Redirects happen before rendering the step and before requesting plans (AC-02.22).
- **Negative:**
  - Three keys per country: clearing after payment is two operations, without atomicity. If the tab dies between the two, an orphan `plan` may remain, which is harmless because without `step1` the summary redirects to step 1.
  - The document remains in plain text in `sessionStorage` for the duration of the quote (risk accepted in G2).
  - The guards wait for an HTTP request: the first navigation by direct URL to `/plans` or `/summary` shows the global "cargando" before the step's.
  - There are two places that evaluate `isComplete` (guard and page after a retry); this is mitigated by using the same pure function.
  - Paying in a duplicated tab is not prevented (accepted limitation, REQ-03.23).
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *Exact names of the `ResourceRef` signals:* the `httpResource` guide documents `value()`, `hasValue()`, `error()` and `isLoading()`. The Angular Developer confirms the reload method in the `ResourceRef` reference before implementing it.
  - *The write `effect()` runs with the initial model and overwrites what was stored before reconciling:* the model is initialized with the already reconciled values, so the first write is idempotent. A unit test verifies it (AC-01.21).

### Confirmation

- Unit: `reconcileStep1` (AC-01.23, AC-01.24), `evaluateStep1` (AC-01.29), `WizardStorage` (corrupted JSON, unexpected types, separation by country: AC-01.22), guards (AC-02.22, AC-03.18, AC-03.30), `SummaryStepPage` with `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS = 0` and an attempt counter (AC-03.22, AC-03.23), `createQuoteNumber` (AC-03.27).
- E2E: AC-01.4, AC-01.21, AC-02.19, AC-02.20, AC-02.30, AC-03.10, AC-03.11, AC-03.28, AC-03.29.
- Review: `grep -rn "localStorage\|serviceWorker\|isComplete.*setItem" frontend/src` with no results; the only `sessionStorage` calls are in `core/storage/`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### P1. One key per country and per data item (chosen)

- For: isolated corruption; clear owner per story; easy to inspect in the e2e tests (AC-01.29: "no completed flag stored").
- Against: several writes when clearing; more keys.

### P2. One object per country

- For: a single write and an atomic clear.
- Against: if the JSON is corrupted the whole country is lost, not just step 1 (table 5.4 says "everything from step 1"). Each story rewrites the whole object, which couples the three.

### P3. State library with persistence

- For: ready-made patterns (hydration, selectors).
- Against: a new dependency without real need (`CLAUDE.md` §6); the state is small.

### L1. `resource()` + `CmsClient` (chosen)

- For: stable in v22; the asynchronous *loader* allows paginating and mapping in a single step; cancels when destroyed.
- Against: adds a level of indirection compared to `httpResource`.

### L2. `httpResource()`

- For: very concise; uses `HttpClient` (with interceptors); `parse` option for validation.
- Against: one URL per resource. Walking the pages (REQ-02.24) and combining the configuration requests (country + fields) requires composing several resources by hand.

### L3. `HttpClient` + manual signals

- For: full control and a very well-known API.
- Against: reimplements cancellation, state and reload in every page, with more surface for errors in the loading states.

### G1. Functional guards (chosen)

- For: the redirect happens before activating the component, so no plans are requested (AC-02.22). It is the idiomatic Angular mechanism.
- Against: a global pending-navigation indicator is needed; a guard that fails to load must let the navigation through.

### G2. Check in the page

- For: the loading state is local and natural.
- Against: the component gets activated and could request plans before deciding; the access logic is spread across pages.

## References

Consulted on 2026-11-22:

- Angular, `resource()` (stable since v22.0, cancellation with `AbortSignal`): https://angular.dev/api/core/resource
- Angular, `httpResource` (stable since v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/common/http/httpResource
- Angular, `httpResource` guide (`value`, `hasValue`, `error`, `isLoading`, `parse`, interceptors): https://angular.dev/guide/http/http-resource
- Angular, guards (`CanActivateFn`, `RedirectCommand`): https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards
- Angular, zoneless by default (v21+), zoneless `TestBed`: https://angular.dev/guide/zoneless
- MDN, `crypto.getRandomValues` (cryptographically strong, also available outside secure contexts): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues
- Strapi 5, pagination (`pagination[page]`, `pagination[pageSize]`, `meta.pagination.pageCount`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/sort-pagination

- **From the summary** (REQ-03.9 to REQ-03.11): "edit data" → `/form`; from there continue → `/plans` with the plan preselected → `/summary`.
- **Focus when changing step** (REQ-01.31, REQ-02.28, REQ-03.33): each page focuses its `<h1 tabindex="-1">` with `afterNextRender`, and the shell updates `document.title` with the step title (Strapi text).

### Simulated payment and confirmation (D9, G2-12)

- Local state of `SummaryStepPage`, not persisted:
  - `termsAccepted = signal(false)`
  - `outcome = signal<'approved' | 'rejected'>('approved')`
  - `payment = signal<'idle' | 'processing' | 'rejected'>('idle')`
- `canPay = computed(...)` with the data loaded and valid, the plan valid, the terms loaded and accepted, and `payment() !== 'processing'` (REQ-03.19).
- `pay()` returns immediately if `payment() === 'processing'`. This is the **guard in the state**, independent of the `disabled` attribute (REQ-03.23). Then it changes the state to `processing` and calls `MockPaymentGateway.pay(outcome, abortSignal)`, which resolves after `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS` (token, 1500 ms by default; REQ-03.24). It makes no request (REQ-03.20).
- When the page is destroyed, the pending payment is aborted (`DestroyRef`) and its result is ignored (REQ-03.22).
- **Success**, in this order:
  1. Generates the number with `createQuoteNumber(cc, now, randomSource)`, a pure function with `crypto.getRandomValues` injected (REQ-03.26).
  2. Writes `confirmation`.
  3. Clears `step1` and `plan`.
  4. Navigates to `/:country/confirmation` with `replaceUrl: true`.

  If the user goes back afterwards, the summary redirects to an empty step 1 because `isComplete` is false (REQ-03.28, AC-03.29).
- **Rejection:** `payment.set('rejected')`, message with `role="alert"`; the data and the terms acceptance are kept (REQ-03.30).
- **New quote:** clears `confirmation` and navigates to `/:country/form`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Each key has a single owner and a clear life cycle. If a key is corrupted, only that one is lost (e.g. step 1), as 5.4 requires.
  - `isComplete` cannot become stale because it does not exist in storage (F-00.5).
  - `resource()` provides cancellation via `AbortSignal` when leaving the page or reloading, and a uniform state for loading, error and retry.
  - Redirects happen before rendering the step and before requesting plans (AC-02.22).
- **Negative:**
  - Three keys per country: clearing after payment is two operations, without atomicity. If the tab dies between the two, an orphan `plan` may remain, which is harmless because without `step1` the summary redirects to step 1.
  - The document remains in plain text in `sessionStorage` for the duration of the quote (risk accepted in G2).
  - The guards wait for an HTTP request: the first navigation by direct URL to `/plans` or `/summary` shows the global "cargando" before the step's.
  - There are two places that evaluate `isComplete` (guard and page after a retry); this is mitigated by using the same pure function.
  - Paying in a duplicated tab is not prevented (accepted limitation, REQ-03.23).
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *Exact names of the `ResourceRef` signals:* the `httpResource` guide documents `value()`, `hasValue()`, `error()` and `isLoading()`. The Angular Developer confirms the reload method in the `ResourceRef` reference before implementing it.
  - *The write `effect()` runs with the initial model and overwrites what was stored before reconciling:* the model is initialized with the already reconciled values, so the first write is idempotent. A unit test verifies it (AC-01.21).

### Confirmation

- Unit: `reconcileStep1` (AC-01.23, AC-01.24), `evaluateStep1` (AC-01.29), `WizardStorage` (corrupted JSON, unexpected types, separation by country: AC-01.22), guards (AC-02.22, AC-03.18, AC-03.30), `SummaryStepPage` with `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS = 0` and an attempt counter (AC-03.22, AC-03.23), `createQuoteNumber` (AC-03.27).
- E2E: AC-01.4, AC-01.21, AC-02.19, AC-02.20, AC-02.30, AC-03.10, AC-03.11, AC-03.28, AC-03.29.
- Review: `grep -rn "localStorage\|serviceWorker\|isComplete.*setItem" frontend/src` with no results; the only `sessionStorage` calls are in `core/storage/`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### P1. One key per country and per data item (chosen)

- For: isolated corruption; clear owner per story; easy to inspect in the e2e tests (AC-01.29: "no completed flag stored").
- Against: several writes when clearing; more keys.

### P2. One object per country

- For: a single write and an atomic clear.
- Against: if the JSON is corrupted the whole country is lost, not just step 1 (table 5.4 says "everything from step 1"). Each story rewrites the whole object, which couples the three.

### P3. State library with persistence

- For: ready-made patterns (hydration, selectors).
- Against: a new dependency without real need (`CLAUDE.md` §6); the state is small.

### L1. `resource()` + `CmsClient` (chosen)

- For: stable in v22; the asynchronous *loader* allows paginating and mapping in a single step; cancels when destroyed.
- Against: adds a level of indirection compared to `httpResource`.

### L2. `httpResource()`

- For: very concise; uses `HttpClient` (with interceptors); `parse` option for validation.
- Against: one URL per resource. Walking the pages (REQ-02.24) and combining the configuration requests (country + fields) requires composing several resources by hand.

### L3. `HttpClient` + manual signals

- For: full control and a very well-known API.
- Against: reimplements cancellation, state and reload in every page, with more surface for errors in the loading states.

### G1. Functional guards (chosen)

- For: the redirect happens before activating the component, so no plans are requested (AC-02.22). It is the idiomatic Angular mechanism.
- Against: a global pending-navigation indicator is needed; a guard that fails to load must let the navigation through.

### G2. Check in the page

- For: the loading state is local and natural.
- Against: the component gets activated and could request plans before deciding; the access logic is spread across pages.

## References

Consulted on 2026-11-22:

- Angular, `resource()` (stable since v22.0, cancellation with `AbortSignal`): https://angular.dev/api/core/resource
- Angular, `httpResource` (stable since v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/common/http/httpResource
- Angular, `httpResource` guide (`value`, `hasValue`, `error`, `isLoading`, `parse`, interceptors): https://angular.dev/guide/http/http-resource
- Angular, guards (`CanActivateFn`, `RedirectCommand`): https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards
- Angular, zoneless by default (v21+), zoneless `TestBed`: https://angular.dev/guide/zoneless
- MDN, `crypto.getRandomValues` (cryptographically strong, also available outside secure contexts): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues
- Strapi 5, pagination (`pagination[page]`, `pagination[pageSize]`, `meta.pagination.pageCount`): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/sort-pagination

1	# ADR-0005 — Regla de precio configurable: factores por país y función pura
2	
3	| Campo | Valor |
4	|---|---|
5	| Estado | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
6	| Fecha | 2026-11-22 |
7	| Autor | Software Architect (subagente) |
8	| Decisores | Humano (G3) |
9	| Motivado por | D8 · G2-1, G2-8, G2-9, G2-13 · REQ-02.6, REQ-02.8, REQ-02.9, REQ-02.10, REQ-02.11, REQ-02.12, REQ-02.13, REQ-02.23, REQ-03.4, REQ-03.5 |
10	
11	## Contexto y problema
12	
13	El PDF dice: "The final price may be adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data. The rule is documented." D8 fijó factores por país en Strapi más una función pura, y G2-8 aprobó el algoritmo: `Math.round(basePrice × Π multiplicadores)`, con operandos `vehicleAge` y `ageInYears`, bandas inclusivas por país y enlace por rol (G2-1). Falta decidir cómo se modelan los factores en Strapi, la firma exacta de la función y cómo se comparte entre el paso 2 y el resumen (G2-9). La documentación pedida por REQ-02.13 está en [`docs/architecture/pricing-rule.md`](../architecture/pricing-rule.md).
14	
15	## Factores de decisión
16	
17	- El negocio cambia bandas, multiplicadores, orden y el rol al que aplican sin código (REQ-02.9).
18	- "Primera banda en el orden configurado" (REQ-02.12): el orden tiene que ser explícito y fácil de editar.
19	- Los factores se piden en cada entrada al paso 2 y al resumen (REQ-02.23, REQ-03.5), sin pedir de nuevo los textos.
20	- Función pura y determinista con fecha inyectada (REQ-02.8).
21	- El mismo resultado en el paso 2 y en el resumen (REQ-03.5).
22	
23	## Opciones consideradas
24	
25	1. **Componente repetible `pricing.price-factor` dentro de `Country`** (`priceFactors`), en el orden del array.
26	2. **Colección `price-factor`** con relación a `Country` y un campo `order`.
27	3. **Campo JSON** `priceRules` en `Country`.
28	
29	## Decisión
30	
31	Opción elegida: **1. Componente repetible en `Country`**.
32	
33	**Modelo (Strapi):**
34	
35	| Atributo | Tipo | Obligatorio | Notas |
36	|---|---|---|---|
37	| `role` | enumeration `vehicleYear`, `birthDate` | Sí | Roles de US-01 que usa la regla (G2-1) |
38	| `operand` | enumeration `vehicleAge`, `ageInYears` | Sí | Operandos fijos en código (G2-8) |
39	| `min` | integer | No | Vacío = sin límite inferior |
40	| `max` | integer | No | Vacío = sin límite superior |
41	| `multiplier` | decimal | Sí | Debe ser > 0 y finito |
42	
43	Se piden con una proyección que no incluye los textos: `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]={cc}&fields[0]=code&populate[0]=priceFactors` (C6 en api-contracts).
44	
45	**Funciones puras** (`frontend/src/app/domain/pricing/`):
46	
47	```ts
48	export type PriceRole = 'vehicleYear' | 'birthDate';
49	export type PriceOperand = 'vehicleAge' | 'ageInYears';
50	export interface PriceFactorRule { role: PriceRole; operand: PriceOperand; min: number | null; max: number | null; multiplier: number; }
51	export interface PriceInputs { vehicleYear: number | null; birthDate: string | null; } // valores por rol, desde Step1Result
52	export interface AppliedFactor { role: PriceRole; operand: PriceOperand; x: number | null; multiplier: number; }
53	export function computeFinalPrice(basePrice: number, inputs: PriceInputs, rules: readonly PriceFactorRule[], referenceDate: string /* YYYY-MM-DD */): { finalPrice: number; appliedFactors: AppliedFactor[] };
54	export function formatPrice(amount: number, intlLocale: string, currency: string): string;
55	```
56	
57	- Algoritmo idéntico a US-02 §6.3:
58	  1. Descartar las reglas inválidas.
59	  2. Agrupar por (`role`, `operand`).
60	  3. Calcular `x` (`vehicleAge = max(0, año(ref) − año)`; `ageInYears` con la misma función `ageInYears` que usa la mayoría de edad de US-01, en `domain/dates/`).
61	  4. El factor es la primera banda con `min ≤ x ≤ max` o, si no hay ninguna, 1.
62	  5. `Math.round` una sola vez al final.
63	- **Combinación rol-operando incompatible** (`birthDate` con `vehicleAge` o `vehicleYear` con `ageInYears`): el mapper la descarta con aviso, igual que una banda inválida. Es una extensión de REQ-02.12 que necesita confirmación humana (ver Decisiones para G3).
64	- `PriceInputs` se obtiene por **rol** desde `Step1Result`, nunca por `key` (REQ-02.10). Si hay varios campos con el mismo rol (G2-5 lo permite), se usa el primero en el orden de pantalla. Para el precio no hay ambigüedad práctica, porque todos deben ser válidos para que `isComplete` sea verdadero. Se documenta como regla determinista.
65	- `formatPrice` usa `new Intl.NumberFormat(intlLocale, { style: 'currency', currency, minimumFractionDigits: 0, maximumFractionDigits: 0 })` (REQ-02.6). Fijar 0 decimales es una decisión aprobada en la spec para COP y CLP. Una moneda con decimales exigiría superseder este ADR.
66	- **Compartida por el paso 2 y el resumen:** las dos páginas llaman a `computeFinalPrice` con el mismo `Step1Result`, los mismos factores recién pedidos y `todayLocal(clock())`. Nada de precio se persiste (G2-9).
67	- `basePrice` es `integer` en Strapi (unidades enteras de la moneda, `min: 1`), lo que evita ambigüedades de serialización de los decimales. `multiplier` es `decimal`, y el mapper acepta un `number` o un `string` numérico, y descarta todo lo que no sea finito.
68	
69	## Consecuencias
70	
71	- **Positivas:**
72	  - El negocio edita todas las bandas de un país en una sola pantalla del admin y las reordena arrastrando; el orden es el del array y no hace falta un campo `order`.
73	  - No hay bandas sin país ni bandas de un país en otro: el componente pertenece a `Country`.
74	  - Función pura, tabla E1–E6 como unit test, y el mismo código en el paso 2 y en el resumen.
75	- **Negativas:**
76	  - Cambiar un factor exige volver a publicar `Country` completo (ADR-0001), y un borrador pendiente de textos del mismo país bloquea publicar el factor.
77	  - Se pide `Country` dos veces en un mismo flujo (configuración una vez por carga y factores en cada entrada), con proyecciones distintas.
78	  - `role` y `operand` son redundantes (cada rol tiene un único operando válido). Se conservan porque G2-8 los aprobó así y porque permiten operandos nuevos sobre el mismo rol, pero exigen la regla de descarte de combinaciones incompatibles.
79	  - `basePrice` entero no admite monedas con céntimos.
80	- **Riesgos y mitigación:**
81	  - *Serialización de `decimal` en la REST API* (número o cadena según la base de datos): la documentación consultada no lo precisa. El mapper acepta ambos, y un unit test cubre los dos casos.
82	  - *Bandas que cambian cerca de la fecha del e2e:* el e2e fija el reloj (ADR-0007).
83	
84	### Confirmación
85	
86	- Unit: `computeFinalPrice` con E1–E6, AC-02.10, AC-02.11, AC-02.12 y AC-02.13; `formatPrice` con las cadenas exactas de AC-02.8 (U+00A0 en `es-CO`); mapper de factores (multiplicador 0, `min > max`, combinación incompatible, decimal como cadena).
87	- E2E: AC-02.9 (con reloj fijado), AC-02.16, AC-02.25 (cambio de factor y recarga, ADR-0003) y AC-03.9.
88	- Review: `grep -rn "Math.round" frontend/src/app` → solo en `domain/pricing/`.
89	
90	## Pros y contras de las opciones
91	
92	### 1. Componente repetible en `Country` (elegida)
93	
94	- A favor: orden nativo; edición agrupada por país; ningún documento huérfano; una petición pequeña con proyección.
95	- En contra: se publica con todo el país; redundancia entre rol y operando.
96	
97	### 2. Colección `price-factor`
98	
99	- A favor: publicación por banda; se pide sin tocar `Country`; permisos separados.
100	- En contra: necesita un campo `order` con sus empates y vacíos (otra regla de desempate). Puede haber bandas sin país. Hace falta otro permiso público y otra ruta en la allowlist. El negocio edita bandas sueltas sin ver el conjunto.
101	
102	### 3. Campo JSON
103	
104	- A favor: máxima flexibilidad sin cambiar el esquema.
105	- En contra: el admin no valida nada (un error de sintaxis rompe la regla); no es "configurable por el negocio" en un sentido razonable.
106	
107	## Referencias
108	
109	Consultadas el 2026-11-22:
110	
111	- Strapi 5, populate de componentes (`populate[0]=component-name`) y selección de campos: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select
112	- Strapi 5, tipos de atributo (`integer`, `decimal`, `enumeration`, `component` repetible): https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/models
113	- MDN, constructor `Intl.NumberFormat` (`style: 'currency'`, `currency` obligatorio, `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits`): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat/NumberFormat
114	- Formato de moneda en Node 24.22.3 (`es-CO` → `24 a0 31 2e …`, `es-CL` → `24 33 38 2e …`): `reviews/000-G2-specs-cross-consistency.md` (ejecución real, F-00.6)

# ADR-0004 — Wizard state, data loading, persistence and navigation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | Accepted (2026-11-22, G3) |
| Date | 2026-11-22 |
| Author | Software Architect (subagent) |
| Deciders | Human (G3) |
| Motivated by | D6, D7, D9 · G2-9, G2-10, G2-11, G2-12, G2-13 · REQ-01.3, REQ-01.4, REQ-01.6, REQ-01.18, REQ-01.23 to REQ-01.27, REQ-01.31, REQ-02.16 to REQ-02.23, REQ-02.30, REQ-03.1, REQ-03.5, REQ-03.9 to REQ-03.14, REQ-03.19, REQ-03.21 to REQ-03.32, REQ-03.37 |

## Context and problem

The wizard has 3 steps plus a confirmation (D7) and persists in `sessionStorage`, separated by country (D6). The specs set rules that cut across the three stories:

- Only values are stored; `isComplete` is computed each time with the current configuration and is never persisted (G2-10, F-00.5).
- Only the plan's `documentId` is persisted, and the price is recomputed (G2-9).
- The terms acceptance, the chosen outcome and the payment state are not persisted (US-03 §6.2).
- After a successful payment the country's state is cleared and a minimal confirmation with no personal data remains (REQ-03.28).
- The country configuration is requested once per app load (Q-01.20). Plans and factors, on every entry to step 2 (REQ-02.23) and to the summary (REQ-03.5, REQ-03.14).

We need to decide the storage format and keys, where the state lives, how data is loaded with explicit states, how the guards work and how the payment is protected.

## Decision drivers

- State with `signal`/`computed`, zoneless, no NgModules (D2, `CLAUDE.md` §8).
- Logic in pure functions (reconciliation, `isComplete`, price, masking, quote number).
- Strict separation by country (REQ-01.25, REQ-03.37).
- Tolerance to corrupted or tampered data (US-01 5.4).
- Loading, error and empty states on every call, with "cargando" announced (REQ-01.3, REQ-02.20, REQ-03.31).
- No new dependencies.

## Considered options

**Persistence format**

1. **P1. One key per country and per data type** (`ciq.v1.{cc}.step1`, `.plan`, `.confirmation`), JSON validated on read.
2. **P2. A single object per country** (`ciq.{cc}` with `step1`, `plan`, `confirmation`).
3. **P3. State library with persistence** (e.g. `@ngrx/signals` with a storage plugin).

**Data loading**

1. **L1. Angular `resource()`** (stable since v22) with a *loader* that calls `CmsClient` (`HttpClient`), which paginates and maps.
2. **L2. `httpResource()`** (stable since v22) directly on each URL.
3. **L3. `HttpClient` + hand-written state signals.**

**Navigation guards**

1. **G1. Functional `canActivate` guards** that wait for the country configuration (in memory) and return `RedirectCommand`, plus a "cargando" indicator while navigation is pending.
2. **G2. Check inside each page**, which redirects with `router.navigate(..., { replaceUrl: true })` after loading.

## Decision

Chosen option: **P1 + L1 + G1** (with the G2 check as a fallback after a retry).

### Persistence (P1)

Access through `WizardStorage` (`frontend/src/app/core/storage/`), which receives the `Storage` through a `WIZARD_STORAGE` token (by default `sessionStorage`, replaceable in tests).

| Key | Content (JSON) | Owner | Cleared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.step1` | `{ "values": { "<fieldKey>": string \| number \| boolean \| null } }` | US-01 | After a successful payment |
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` | `{ "planDocumentId": "<documentId>" }` | US-02 | After a successful payment; when discarding an unavailable plan (REQ-02.17) |
| `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` | `{ "quoteNumber": "CO-20261122-7K3F9Q", "planName": "...", "finalPrice": 1320000, "currency": "COP", "paidAt": "2026-11-22T15:04:05.000Z" }` | US-03 | With "new quote" |

- `{cc}` is the already validated lowercase country code from the URL. `v1` is the schema version: if it changes, `v2` is used and the `v1` keys are ignored and removed.
- **Nothing else is stored:** no configuration, plans, prices, factors, terms, `isComplete`, terms acceptance or payment outcome (REQ-01.6, REQ-02.23, G2-9, G2-10, REQ-03.12).
- **Defensive read:** if the JSON cannot be parsed or does not have the expected shape, that key is discarded and a console warning is logged without personal data (5.4). A value of an unexpected type is discarded individually.
- **Step 1 write:** an `effect()` in `DynamicForm` writes the **normalized** values on every model change: trimmed `text`, `NaN` → `null`, `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` (REQ-01.23, Q-01.16). `action` writes again on continue. While typing, the model keeps the untrimmed text, and when leaving the field it is replaced by the trimmed one.
- The document and the birth date remain in plain text in `sessionStorage` (Q-01.15, Q-03.23); this is documented in the README.

### In-memory state

- `CountryConfigStore` (`providedIn: 'root'`) holds a `Map<cc, ResourceRef<CountryConfig>>`. `CountryConfig` = country + texts + `FormConfig`. It is created when entering the country and **is not requested again** when navigating between steps, only on reload or when pressing "reintentar" (Q-01.20).
- `Step1State` derives from the storage and the configuration:
  - `reconcileStep1(config, stored) → Step1Model`: pure function with table 5.4.
  - `evaluateStep1(config, values, { today, minimumAge }) → Step1Result`: pure function. For each current field it returns `key`, `type`, `section`, `role`, `value`, `displayValue` (option label for `select`) and `valid`, plus `isComplete` (REQ-01.27). `isComplete` is `false` if the configuration is not `ready` (empty, unavailable or with an error).
  - `isComplete` is a `computed` over those functions: it is recomputed when read and never written.
- Plans and factors are requested with a `resource()` created by the page (step 2 and summary), so they are cancelled on leaving and requested again on every entry (REQ-02.23).
- The terms, with their own `resource()` in the summary, to show loading and error in that section (REQ-03.31, REQ-03.32, AC-03.17).

### Data loading (L1) and states

- `CmsClient` (`core/cms/`) makes the `GET` request, applies a **10 000 ms timeout** (REQ-02.21 leaves the value to the ADR), walks the pages if `pageCount > 1` (REQ-02.24), validates the overall shape and delivers DTOs. The mappers convert DTOs into domain objects (api-contracts).
- `resource()` exposes the loading state, the error and the value, and allows reloading. The pages derive a single `viewState`: `loading` | `error` | `configError` (a text is missing, G2-2) | `empty` | `unavailable` (G2-5) | `ready`.
  - `loading` → "cargando" with `role="status"`.
  - `error` → "error de carga" + "reintentar" with `role="alert"`.
  - `configError` → the country's generic message or, if that is also missing, "error de carga" (F-00.7).
- No automatic retries: only the "reintentar" button (REQ-01.4).
- The 4 fixed texts (G2-2) are in a single file, `core/ui-state/fixed-texts.ts`.

### Navigation and guards (G1)

| Route | Guard | Rule | Redirect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/:country` (shell) | `countryCaseGuard` | Uppercase segment | Same URL in lowercase (ADR-0001) |
| `/:country/plans` | `step1CompleteGuard` | Waits for `CountryConfig`. If it is `ready` and `isComplete` is false | `/:country/form`, without requesting plans (REQ-02.19, AC-02.22) |
| `/:country/summary` | `step1CompleteGuard`, `planSelectedGuard` | `isComplete` false → step 1; no `ciq.v1.{cc}.plan` → step 2 | REQ-03.13, AC-03.18 |
| `/:country/confirmation` | `confirmationGuard` | No valid `ciq.v1.{cc}.confirmation` | `/:country/form` (REQ-03.29) |

- The guards return `true` if the configuration **fails** to load. The page then shows "error de carga" and, after a successful "reintentar", evaluates `isComplete` again and redirects if needed (G2 fallback).
- While a guard is waiting, the root component shows "cargando" (a signal derived from `Router` events: `NavigationStart` → `true`; `NavigationEnd`, `NavigationCancel` or `NavigationError` → `false`). This satisfies REQ-02.20 when entering by URL.
- **Plan not available in the summary** (REQ-03.14, G2-11): the summary loads the plans and, if the persisted plan is not in the current list, navigates to `/:country/plans` without clearing anything. Step 2 detects the same case, discards the selection and shows the notice (REQ-02.17). This way there is a single implementation of the discard.
- **From the summary** (REQ-03.9 to REQ-03.11): "edit data" → `/form`; from there continue → `/plans` with the plan preselected → `/summary`.
- **Focus when changing step** (REQ-01.31, REQ-02.28, REQ-03.33): each page focuses its `<h1 tabindex="-1">` with `afterNextRender`, and the shell updates `document.title` with the step title (Strapi text).

### Simulated payment and confirmation (D9, G2-12)

- Local state of `SummaryStepPage`, not persisted:
  - `termsAccepted = signal(false)`
  - `outcome = signal<'approved' | 'rejected'>('approved')`
  - `payment = signal<'idle' | 'processing' | 'rejected'>('idle')`
- `canPay = computed(...)` with the data loaded and valid, the plan valid, the terms loaded and accepted, and `payment() !== 'processing'` (REQ-03.19).
- `pay()` returns immediately if `payment() === 'processing'`. This is the **guard in the state**, independent of the `disabled` attribute (REQ-03.23). Then it changes the state to `processing` and calls `MockPaymentGateway.pay(outcome, abortSignal)`, which resolves after `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS` (token, 1500 ms by default; REQ-03.24). It makes no request (REQ-03.20).
- When the page is destroyed, the pending payment is aborted (`DestroyRef`) and its result is ignored (REQ-03.22).
- **Success**, in this order:
  1. Generates the number with `createQuoteNumber(cc, now, randomSource)`, a pure function with `crypto.getRandomValues` injected (REQ-03.26).
  2. Writes `confirmation`.
  3. Clears `step1` and `plan`.
  4. Navigates to `/:country/confirmation` with `replaceUrl: true`.

  If the user goes back afterwards, the summary redirects to an empty step 1 because `isComplete` is false (REQ-03.28, AC-03.29).
- **Rejection:** `payment.set('rejected')`, message with `role="alert"`; the data and the terms acceptance are kept (REQ-03.30).
- **New quote:** clears `confirmation` and navigates to `/:country/form`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Each key has a single owner and a clear life cycle. If a key is corrupted, only that one is lost (e.g. step 1), as 5.4 requires.
  - `isComplete` cannot become stale because it does not exist in storage (F-00.5).
  - `resource()` provides cancellation via `AbortSignal` when leaving the page or reloading, and a uniform state for loading, error and retry.
  - Redirects happen before rendering the step and before requesting plans (AC-02.22).
- **Negative:**
  - Three keys per country: clearing after payment is two operations, without atomicity. If the tab dies between the two, an orphan `plan` may remain, which is harmless because without `step1` the summary redirects to step 1.
  - The document remains in plain text in `sessionStorage` for the duration of the quote (risk accepted in G2).
  - The guards wait for an HTTP request: the first navigation by direct URL to `/plans` or `/summary` shows the global "cargando" before the step's.
  - There are two places that evaluate `isComplete` (guard and page after a retry); this is mitigated by using the same pure function.
  - Paying in a duplicated tab is not prevented (accepted limitation, REQ-03.23).
- **Risks and mitigation:**
  - *Exact names of the `ResourceRef` signals:* the `httpResource` guide documents `value()`, `hasValue()`, `error()` and `isLoading()`. The Angular Developer confirms the reload method in the `ResourceRef` reference before implementing it.
  - *The write `effect()` runs with the initial model and overwrites what was stored before reconciling:* the model is initialized with the already reconciled values, so the first write is idempotent. A unit test verifies it (AC-01.21).

### Confirmation

- Unit: `reconcileStep1` (AC-01.23, AC-01.24), `evaluateStep1` (AC-01.29), `WizardStorage` (corrupted JSON, unexpected types, separation by country: AC-01.22), guards (AC-02.22, AC-03.18, AC-03.30), `SummaryStepPage` with `PAYMENT_DELAY_MS = 0` and an attempt counter (AC-03.22, AC-03.23), `createQuoteNumber` (AC-03.27).
- E2E: AC-01.4, AC-01.21, AC-02.19, AC-02.20, AC-02.30, AC-03.10, AC-03.11, AC-03.28, AC-03.29.
- Review: `grep -rn "localStorage\|serviceWorker\|isComplete.*setItem" frontend/src` with no results; the only `sessionStorage` calls are in `core/storage/`.

## Pros and cons of the options

### P1. One key per country and per data item (chosen)

- For: isolated corruption; clear owner per story; easy to inspect in the e2e tests (AC-01.29: "no completed flag stored").
- Against: several writes when clearing; more keys.

### P2. One object per country

- For: a single write and an atomic clear.
- Against: if the JSON is corrupted the whole country is lost, not just step 1 (table 5.4 says "everything from step 1"). Each story rewrites the whole object, which couples the three.

### P3. State library with persistence

- For: ready-made patterns (hydration, selectors).
- Against: a new dependency without real need (`CLAUDE.md` §6); the state is small.

### L1. `resource()` + `CmsClient` (chosen)

- For: stable in v22; the asynchronous *loader* allows paginating and mapping in a single step; cancels when destroyed.
- Against: adds a level of indirection compared to `httpResource`.

### L2. `httpResource()`

- For: very concise; uses `HttpClient` (with interceptors); `parse` option for validation.
- Against: one URL per resource. Walking the pages (REQ-02.24) and combining the configuration requests (country + fields) requires composing several resources by hand.

### L3. `HttpClient` + manual signals

- For: full control and a very well-known API.
- Against: reimplements cancellation, state and reload in every page, with more surface for errors in the loading states.

### G1. Functional guards (chosen)

- For: the redirect happens before activating the component, so no plans are requested (AC-02.22). It is the idiomatic Angular mechanism.
- Against: a global pending-navigation indicator is needed; a guard that fails to load must let the navigation through.

### G2. Check in the page

- For: the loading state is local and natural.
- Against: the component gets activated and could request plans before deciding; the access logic is spread across pages.

## References

Consulted on 2026-11-22:

- Angular, `resource()` (stable since v22.0, cancellation with `AbortSignal`): https://angular.dev/api/core/resource
- Angular, `httpResource` (stable since v22.0): https://angular.dev/api/common/http/httpResource
- Angular, `httpResource` guide (`value`, `hasValue`, `error`, `isLoading`, `parse`, interceptors): https://angular.dev/guide/http/http-resource
- Angular, guards (`CanActivateFn`, `RedirectCommand`): https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards
- Angular, zoneless by default (v21+), zoneless `TestBed`: https://angular.dev/guide/zoneless
- MDN, `crypto.getRandomValues` (cryptographically strong, also available outside secure contexts): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues
